stories.title: Embiid has season-high 37 and Brown adds 31 as 76ers beat Nets 135-123 without LeBron James
stories.summary: — Joel Embiid scored a season-high 37 points, Jaylen Brown matched his season best with 31 and the superstars provided the Philadelphia 76ers with more than enough in LeBron James' absence to beat the Brooklyn Nets 135-123 on Monday night.
stories.detailText: NEW YORK -- — Joel Embiid scored a season-high 37 points, Jaylen Brown matched his season best with 31 and the superstars provided the Philadelphia 76ers with more than enough in LeBron James ' absence to beat the Brooklyn Nets 135-123 on Monday night. Brown added 13 rebounds but wasn't in the game for the finish after a collision with Julius Randle in the fourth quarter opened a cut on his head. Brown returned to the game wearing a headband after being treated, but then left again a few minutes later. James sat out on the second half of the 76ers' back-to-back games and Philadelphia improved to 4-0 without him. Tyrese Maxey finished with 24 points and nine assists. Embiid had 24 points by halftime of what appeared would be a blowout. The Nets made it a game in the fourth quarter before the center helped turn them back, scoring six straight Philadelphia points to extend a six-point lead back into double figures and then making a 3-pointer with 51 seconds remaining after Brooklyn had climbed back within four. Julius Randle scored 33 points and Michael Porter Jr . added 25 for the Nets, who fell to 3-10. Second-year guard Nolan Traore matched his career high with 23 points. Embiid sat out the victory Sunday over Indiana in which James passed Jason Kidd to move into No. 3 on the NBA's career assists list. The 76ers didn't officially list Embiid as available Monday until about half an hour before the game, but it was clear he was fine. He had 13 points in the first quarter as Philadelphia took a 33-26 lead. The Sixers made their first three shots in the second, and when they finally missed, Dean Wade dunked the rebound while being fouled for a three-point play and a 46-28 lead. They made nine of their first 11 shots in the period — and scored on the rebound of that second miss as well. The lead reached 63-39 on Maxey's 3-pointer before Philadelphia took a 78-59 lead to halftime. The Nets charged back into the game in the third, cutting it to 105-95 headed to the fourth. Randle's 3-pointer trimmed it to 106-101 early in the period. Up next 76ers: Visit Orlando on Wednesday. Nets: Host Chicago on Wednesday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

stories.title: Bane scores 24, Magic rally in 4th quarter to beat Celtics 115-105, extend win streak to 4 games
stories.summary: — Desmond Bane had 24 points and eight rebounds to help the Orlando Magic rally in the fourth quarter and earn their fourth consecutive victory, 115-105 over the Boston Celtics on Monday night.
stories.detailText: BOSTON -- — Desmond Bane had 24 points and eight rebounds to help the Orlando Magic rally in the fourth quarter and earn their fourth consecutive victory, 115-105 over the Boston Celtics on Monday night. Franz Wagner , who entered the night having scored 30 or more points in each of Orlando’s previous four games, had 21 points, nine assists and eight rebounds. Anthony Black finished with 20 points and seven assists. The Magic shot 50% (41 of 82) from the field in the game to earn their first win in Boston since Dec. 18, 2022. It was Boston's first home loss of the season and snapped the team's six-game win streak. Jayson Tatum led the Celtics with 24 points and 12 rebounds, his first double-double since their season-opening loss at Detroit. But he also had five of his team’s 11 turnovers. Paul George added 22 points and Payton Pritchard had 21 points. The Magic, despite playing on three days of rest, struggled with their shot early. But they still managed to cobble together a 50-41 lead at halftime. Playing on the second night of a back-to-back, the Celtics showed some early signs of fatigue. But they found some traction in the third quarter, led by Tatum’s 14 points to outscore Orlando 36-25 in the period and take a 77-75 lead into the fourth. But the Magic recovered and got an alley-oop from Wagner to Wendell Carter Jr ., followed by a jumper by Bane to take a 110-99 edge with 1:33 left. A night after finishing the first quarter with a franchise-high 33-point lead in its blowout win over Dallas, Boston needed a 3-pointer at the buzzer by Pritchard to even make it to 17 points by the end of the first period on Monday. Both teams had trouble scoring in the opening quarter. The Magic went 7 of 21 (33.3%) from the field, while the Celtics made only 6 of 24 (25%) shots. Up next Magic: Host Philadelphia on Wednesday night. Celtics: Visit Denver on Wednesday night. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

stories.title: Heat star Bam Adebayo exits win over Rockets early with hip tightness
stories.summary: Heat star Bam Adebayo was ruled out of Monday's win over the Rockets after 16 first-half minutes due to hip tightness.
stories.detailText: MIAMI -- Heat star big man Bam Adebayo left Monday's 128-110 win over the Houston Rockets with hip tightness and did not return. Adebayo played 16 minutes in the first half and subbed out with 33 seconds left in the second quarter. He did not start the second half and was not seen on the Heat bench for the rest of the game. Andrew Wiggins replaced Adebayo in the starting lineup on Monday. Miami's depth came alive Monday night with seven players scoring in double figures. Giannis Antetokounmpo praised Adebayo as "one of the most versatile bigs I've ever played with" as his partner put up 37 points and 14 rebounds in Friday's win over Cavs. Adebayo is the anchor of the Heat's defense and entered Monday's game averaging 19.5 points, 8.5 rebounds and a career-high 2.1 steals per game. The 8-6 Heat have surged over the past two weeks, winning five straight games behind the duo of Antetokounmpo and Adebayo.

stories.title: 76ers' Jaylen Brown goes down, returns to game vs. Nets with bandage after knocking heads with Julius Randle
stories.summary: Brown and Randle collided in the fourth quarter of Philadelphia's 135-123 win, leaving both men bleeding.
stories.detailText: Philadelphia 76ers forward Jaylen Brown briefly went down with a potential head injury after knocking heads with Brooklyn Nets forward Julius Randle. Though Brown was bleeding, he eventually returned to the game with a bandage on his head, and played a few more minutes of the 76ers’ 135-123 win over the Nets. The collision between Brown and Randle happened in the fourth quarter of Monday’s matchup in Brooklyn, with Brown’s forehead connecting with Randle’s mouth. Both men were bleeding after the incident, though from different parts of the head. A scary collision leaves Jaylen Brown bloodied after contact with Julius Randle. pic.twitter.com/cYhjnvMWsH — NBC Sports Philadelphia (@NBCSPhilly) November 17, 2026 Brown stayed down for a while, rolling onto his back and covering his face with his hands. The entire 76ers bench soon came out to surround him while he was tended to by trainers. Brown then received additional care on the bench, before returning to the game with a bandage on his head. Jaylen Brown just put this headband on then pretended to be a ninja to the Sixers bench pic.twitter.com/LC2BhY6yr7 — Kris Rhim (@krisrhim1) November 17, 2026 Randle, meanwhile, got his bleeding lip stitched up off-court and returned to the game as well. Randle was called for the foul on the play, but because it wasn’t a shooting foul, Brown did not need to attempt free throws. At the time of the foul, Brown had scored 29 points and picked up 12 rebounds, thanks to a first-half double-double. He finished with 31 points, 13 rebounds and four assists in the 12-point victory. Joel Embiid led both teams with 37 points, while Randle had 33 points for Brooklyn in the loss.

stories.title: Giannis Antetokounmpo scores 20, Heat roll past Rockets 128-110 for 5th straight win
stories.summary: — Giannis Antetokounmpo scored 20 points and grabbed 13 rebounds, Andrew Wiggins and Klay Thompson each scored 17 and the Miami Heat never trailed on the way to beating the Houston Rockets 128-110 on Monday night for their fifth straight victory.
stories.detailText: MIAMI -- — Giannis Antetokounmpo scored 20 points and grabbed 13 rebounds, Andrew Wiggins and Klay Thompson each scored 17 and the Miami Heat never trailed on the way to beating the Houston Rockets 128-110 on Monday night for their fifth straight victory. Davion Mitchell had a 16-point, 10-assist night and Bobby Portis Jr. scored 16 points for the Heat, who have gone 8-2 since starting the season 0-4. Miami was without Bam Adebayo for the second half because of right hip tightness. Thompson made five 3-pointers for the Heat, giving him 2,952 for his career and moving him within 21 of Ray Allen (2,973) for third on the all-time 3s list. Antetokounmpo added six assists — and will now face his former team, the Milwaukee Bucks , for the first time on Wednesday. Alperen Sengun scored 23 points for the Rockets, who were on the second night of a back-to-back and saw their four-game winning streak end. Kevin Durant scored 22 for Houston; he's now up to 32,917 points in his career, 83 shy of the 33,000-point milestone. Only four players — LeBron James , Kareem Abdul-Jabbar, Karl Malone and Kobe Bryant — have scored that many. Houston scored a season-high 147 points against Washington on Sunday night. Things went a little differently on Monday. The Rockets started 1 for 9 from the field and scored only two points in the first 5:54 against the Heat, setting the tone for a night where Houston played uphill the whole way. It was Houston's first loss in six games against Eastern Conference teams this season. The top eight teams in the Western Conference, entering Monday, were 22-3 against teams from the East — winning by an average of 13.4 points. None of those teams had lost to an East opponent by more than 11, before Monday. Up next Rockets: Visit Indiana on Wednesday night. Heat: Host Milwaukee on Wednesday night. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

stories.title: Heat star Bam Adebayo leaves win over Rockets early with hip injury
stories.summary: Despite losing Bam Adebayo in the second half, the Heat still rolled to a 128-110 win over the Rockets on Monday night.
stories.detailText: Bam Adebayo left Monday night's contest against the Houston Rockets early with an apparent hip injury. The Miami Heat star did not take the court to start the second half of their 128-110 win over the Rockets at the Kaseya Center on Monday, and was instead replaced by Andrew Wiggins to open the third quarter. It didn't appear as if anything happened to Adebayo in the first half, but he was not spotted on the bench as play resumed. Eventually, the Heat said he was questionable to return with right hip tightness. They then ruled him out for good in the fourth quarter. Further specifics of the injury are not yet known. Adebayo finished the night with just four points and two assists while shooting 1-of-3 from the field. He entered the night averaging 19.5 points and 8.5 rebounds per contest this season. Heat coach Erik Spoelstra said after the game that the team was being “proactive” in holding Adebayo out, and that he didn’t expect it to be a long-term issue for Adebayo, according to the Miami Herald’s Anthony Chiang . While they don’t have specifics just yet, losing Adebayo for an extended amount of time would undoubtedly make a major impact on the Heat. But despite losing him, the Heat still managed to roll to a convincing win over the Rockets. Miami led nearly the entire way on Monday night. The Heat carried a 16-point lead into the locker room at halftime and just cruised the rest of the way to secure the 18-point win. Giannis Antetokounmpo led the way with 20 points, 16 rebounds and six assists. Klay Thompson added 17 points after going 5-of-10 from the 3-point line, and Wiggins had 17 points and five rebounds after stepping in for Adebayo in the second half. The Heat have now won five straight, and sit at 8-6 on the season. Alperen Sengun led the Rockets with 23 points and seven rebounds. Kevin Durant finished with 22 points, and Jabari Smith Jr. had 12 points and 10 rebounds. The loss dropped them to 11-4 on the year.

stories.title: Mitchell and Allen power the Cavaliers to a 126-115 win over the Bulls
stories.summary: — Donovan Mitchell scored 39 points and Jarrett Allen added 13 points and 14 rebounds as the Cleveland Cavaliers overcame an early deficit and beat the Chicago Bulls 126-115 on Monday night.
stories.detailText: CLEVELAND -- — Donovan Mitchell scored 39 points and Jarrett Allen added 13 points and 14 rebounds as the Cleveland Cavaliers overcame an early deficit and beat the Chicago Bulls 126-115 on Monday night. Cleveland trailed by six points, 31-25, after one period before rebounding in the second. The Cavaliers used a 32-17 scoring edge in the second quarter for a 57-48 advantage at the break. Cleveland maintained its nine-point lead through the third quarter and weathered a fourth quarter comeback try by the Bulls to win for the third time in four games. Tyrese Proctor scored 10 of his 17 points in the first half for Cleveland, which improved to 6-2 at home. Peyton Watson chipped in 14 points, Meleek Thomas added 10 and James Harden finished with nine points and 10 assists. Norman Powell led Chicago with 27 points, and Matas Buzelis scored 23. Jalen Smith posted 17 points and 11 rebounds, while Tre Jones finished with 16 points and Isaac Okoro had 13. The loss halted the Bulls' two-game win streak, which followed an eight-game skid. Chicago fell to 2-6 on the road and 3-10 overall. The Cavaliers were without Evan Mobley , who has a sprained big toe on his right foot. Cleveland says he will be re-evaluated in seven to 10 days. Up next Bulls: At the Brooklyn Nets on Wednesday. Cavaliers: Host the Memphis Grizzlies on Wednesday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

stories.title: Donovan Mitchell’s 39 points help push Cavaliers past Bulls 126-115
stories.summary: The Cavaliers were able to resist any potential Bulls comeback.
stories.detailText: Nov 16, 2026; Cleveland, Ohio, USA; Cleveland Cavaliers guard Donovan Mitchell (45) drives to the basket against Chicago Bulls guard Josh Giddey (3) during the first quarter at Rocket Arena. Mandatory Credit: Ken Blaze-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Cleveland Cavaliers , coming off an exceptional win against the Dallas Mavericks with the reserves, had all fans wondering how the starters would respond. The win on Saturday was driven by intensity, effort, and a team that never let their foot off the gas. The starters for Cleveland against the Bulls had a lesser opponent in front of them; however, the effort felt like an improvement from past games in the early season. Right off the bat, the Cavaliers were honed in offensively by scoring through the paint; within the first few possessions, Jarrett Allen was rim running with little to no resistance. Cleveland kept with this mindset and seemed to prioritize their effort on the glass and scoring inside. This proved to be the correct mindset. The Cavaliers scored scoring 68 of their 126 points around the cup. The Cavs were also outhustling the Bulls on the boards, 51-37. Monday proved another great night for the young bucks in Tyrese Proctor and Meleek Thomas. Proctor, who was the star of Saturday night’s game, was given the nod with the starters in the absence of Evan Mobley. Proctor fit in seamlessly with the starters, scoring 17 points and finding his spots without hijacking the offense. Thomas (9 points and 6 rebounds) likewise was able to find his spots and continues to impress. His knack for scoring from almost anywhere on the court allows him to fit with any five-man lineup the Cavaliers throw out. At the end of the day, this game was won by Donovan Mitchell, who scored the game-high 39 points on 16-25 shooting. Whenever it felt like the Bulls would attempt to mount a rally, it was Mitchell who would offer his own counterpunch to end the counter. Mitchell’s ability to sense when his buckets were needed was nice to see from the leader of the team. The Bulls, at the end of the day, do not have someone of Mitchell’s caliber who can respond to the nuclear levels of scoring that Donovan can. While not the dominant effort some were hoping for, it is nice that the Cavaliers can win games like this without having to sweat it out until the final buzzer. It isn’t the 30-point blowouts we saw a few years ago, but this feels like a step in the right direction. The Cavaliers look to take this momentum into their next matchup on Wednesday against the Memphis Grizzlies.

stories.title: Cameron Boozer scores 29 and Grizzlies hand the Wizards an 8th straight loss, 136-120
stories.summary: — Memphis rookie Cameron Boozer scored a season-high 29 points in a matchup with top draft pick AJ Dybantsa of Washington, and the Grizzlies rallied from 12 points down to hand the Wizards their eighth straight loss, 136-120 on Monday night.
stories.detailText: WASHINGTON -- — Memphis rookie Cameron Boozer scored a season-high 29 points in a matchup with top draft pick AJ Dybantsa of Washington, and the Grizzlies rallied from 12 points down to hand the Wizards their eighth straight loss, 136-120 on Monday night. Playing without leading scorer Ty Jerome , who has a sore right hip, the Grizzlies trailed 69-57 in the closing seconds of the first half but took control by outscoring the Wizards 42-18 in the third quarter. Boozer, the No. 3 pick in the draft after a standout season at Duke, finished 7 of 13 on 3-pointers, including two 3s during a 10-0 run that tied the game at 73-all. Zach Edey had 23 points and 10 rebounds for the Grizzlies, who have won four of five and improved to 7-0 on the road. Javon Small had 12 points and 12 assists. Dybantsa matched his season high with 21 points. Washington hasn't won since beating Orlando on Nov. 2 to move to 4-3, and the skid has raised questions about the future of coach Brian Keefe. After a multiyear rebuild, the Wizards hoped to contend this season with veterans Anthony Davis and Trae Young playing alongside Dybantsa. Davis led the Wizards with 23 points. Young, held scoreless for the first time in his career in Sunday night’s 147-119 loss to visiting Houston, had 13 points on 3-of-10 shooting and 12 assists. Young had 10 assists by halftime, the first Wizards player to do that since Tyus Jones on March 10, 2024 at Miami. The only other player with 10 assists in a half this season was Atlanta's Jalen Johnson on Oct. 26 against Houston. The Grizzlies, who entered the game fourth in the NBA in offensive rating, shot 55.8% from the field. Up next Grizzlies: At Cleveland on Wednesday night. Wizards: At Toronto on Wednesday night. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

stories.summary: The Cavs will be without Mobley for the short-term future.

(Photo by Jacob Kupferman/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Cavaliers have announced that NBA All-Star Evan Mobley will be out for the next few games following a left great toe sprain suffered on November 11. Mobley sustained his injury against the New York Knicks. Mobley will be re-evaluated after 7-10 days. The Cavs’ big man is averaging 16.9 points, 7.3 rebounds, 3.6 assists, 1.5 blocks, and 1.1 steals per game. He’s also shooting a career-high 47.9% from the three-point line. Mobley’s increased floor spacing has been his biggest positive development at the start of the season. Mobley isn’t the only Cavalier who has been banged up. Sam Merrill is out with an elbow injury, Jaylon Tyson has been working through an ankle injury, and Nae’Qwan Tomlin has yet to make his season debut with a back injury. These injuries have opened the door for younger players like Meleek Thomas and Tyrese Proctor to rack up early minutes. This has paid off, with both Proctor and Thomas making the most of their increased opportunities. Norchad Omier is another player who deserves credit in this regard. Still, the Cavs haven’t been able to play with much consistency given the changes in their lineup on a nightly basis. This has led to a slower start than fans would like, with Cleveland posting a 7-7 record in their first 14 games. Wins over the Dallas Mavericks with a depleted roster are encouraging. Losses to the Charlotte Hornets are not as much fun. Cleveland has much to figure out this regular season, and injuries won’t make that any easier for them. For now, the Cavs will be without Mobley for at least the next week, which includes games against the Memphis Grizzlies, Indiana Pacers, and another game against the Chicago Bulls next Monday. Mobley’s presence as an all-world defender and elite play finisher will be missed. But the Cavs will lean heavily on Jarrett Allen to hold down the fort in his absence, and an emphasis will be placed on Mario Hezonja and Thomas Bryant to step up and add further support.

Hopefully this is just all a part of the normal stagger. The Sixers released the injury report for their second leg of this back-to-back against the Brooklyn Nets Monday and have listed Joel Embiid as questionable and LeBron James as out. The same reasons have been listed, right plantar fascia management and lower back/sciatica management, respectively. The Sixers have an injury report for tonight's game in Brooklyn: Dominick Barlow – back – OUT Adem Bona – neck – OUT LeBron James – back – OUT Joel Embiid – foot – QUESTIONABLE This is the back end of a back-to-back. — Derek Bodner (@DerekBodnerNBA) November 16, 2026 Nick Nurse said ahead of their win over the Pacers that the team’s load management program is what dictated Embiid missing that game. That would indicate he’d be good to go in Brooklyn, but the questionable designation raises an eyebrow a bit. Nurse also said earlier in the week he thought Embiid wasn’t moving that great in some recent games. The question was also broached to Nurse as to if it’s better to play Embiid and James together in one leg to build chemistry. Nurse says that is something that’s been considered, but the team’s long-term management plans take priority to that. ESPN’s Dave McMenamin just reported that James has asked the Sixers’ coaching staff to be patient with him as he hopes to find his rhythm as the season goes on, hoping for a ramp-up in December. The rest of the injury report hasn’t changed. Adem Bona and Dominick Barlow remain out with their respective neck and back injuries. Brooklyn comes into this one with a clean slate of health. They’re only listings on the injury report are two-way assignments, which includes the No. 28 overall pick in this past year’s draft Joshua Jefferson, as well as 2025 first-round picks Ben Saraf and Drake Powell. Should Embiid be able to go, this should be an easy win for Philadelphia. If he’s not able to, things will get really tricky at the center position without James as an option there either.

stories.title: Jayson Tatum reopens Steve Kerr’s Olympic controversy with ‘fishy s–t’ quote
stories.summary: Jayson Tatum is well into the prime of his career and is considered one of the NBA’s modern superstar players. But two years ago, Golden State Warriors’ head coach Steve...
stories.detailText: Jayson Tatum is well into the prime of his career and is considered one of the NBA’s modern superstar players. But two years ago, Golden State Warriors’ head coach Steve Kerr viewed him as more of an afterthought . During the 2024 Paris Olympics, Tatum was benched in favor of Kevin Durant, who used to play under Steve Kerr, forcing Tatum to spend most of the Summer Olympics on the bench. Tatum reflected on the benching during an interview with “Boardroom” and said Kerr told him he needed to be patient due to Kevin Durant returning to the lineup from a calf injury. Steve Kerr reacting to a call during an NBA game. Getty Images “He was like, ‘You know, Kevin is back. We’re gonna need to try and figure something out with the lineup. But just be patient.’ The f— does that mean?” Tatum said after he was processing Kerr’s words to him. “Once I didn’t get in the first quarter, I was like, ‘Oh, some fishy s—t going on.’ That’s when it kind of hit me like, ‘Oh, that’s what he was trying to tell me.'” Jayson Tatum says Steve Kerr benching him was ‘fishy’ “He was like, just be patient. Like, what the fu*k does that mean? Like why you telling me that?.. once I didn’t get in the first quarter, I was like, “Oh, some fishy sh*t going on.” ( @NBA__Courtside ) pic.twitter.com/8vAEp285hl — NBACentral (@TheDunkCentral) November 16, 2026 That year, Tatum only appeared in three of Team USA’s games, and he saw the second-least amount of action, behind Tyrese Haliburton, of the Indiana Pacers. Tatum played a diminished role as Team USA won its fifth consecutive men’s basketball gold medal, averaging 5.3 points, 5.3 rebounds, 1.5 assists and 1 steal in about 17.8 minutes per game. Jayson Tatum says being benched in the Olympics for Kevin Durant was “some fishy s—t” NBAE via Getty Images When Durant came back from his injury, he averaged 22.3 minutes, averaging 13.8 points, 6 rebounds, and 2.3 assists. Two years before the Paris Olympics, Kerr and Tatum’s paths crossed in the NBA Finals. Boston got off to a 2-1 series lead over Golden State, but the Warriors rallied and won three straight to give Kerr and Stephen Curry their fourth NBA title. Steve Kerr responding during an NBA game. Getty Images Tatum’s time to superstardom came in 2024, when the Celtics dominated the Mavericks in the NBA Finals that year, winning Boston their first NBA title since 2008 by knocking Dallas out in five games. Tatum was later crowned as the cover for the video game, “NBA 2K.” After the Olympics ended that summer, Tatum appeared in an interview with The Athletic and called his experience “humbling.” In November 2024, Kerr said he “felt like an idiot not playing” Tatum and was well aware that he played his Celtics teammates at the time, Derrick White and Jrue Holiday, extensively.

stories.summary: Evan Mobley will be out for the next seven to 10 days recovering from a toe sprain.
stories.detailText: The Cleveland Cavaliers will be without Evan Mobley for at least another week. Mobley suffered a right toe sprain last week during their matchup with the New York Knicks and has been sidelined ever since. That injury has since been confirmed, the team announced on Monday afternoon , and he will now undergo treatment over the next seven to 10 days. Mobley went down in the final minutes of the Cavaliers' 115-107 win over the New York Knicks on Wednesday. He tried to get up to block at shot at Madison Square Garden, but ended up slamming to the court hard and awkwardly. He remained down for a moment, clearly shaken up, and he hasn't played since. The play where Evan Mobley hurt his toe. You can see him grab it afterwards and proceeded to hobble up the floor after free throws. pic.twitter.com/aJ8JuQifcr — RealCavsFans.com (@realcavsfans) November 13, 2026 Coach Kenny Atkinson said Friday , ahead of the Cavs' loss to the Miami Heat, that it was just a "sprain" and that they didn't "expect it to be a long-term thing at all." Mobley missed that game and Saturday's win over the Dallas Mavericks as a result. But instead of just a game or two, Mobley will need at least another full week to recover. If he's out just the seven days, he'd be able to return for their matchup with the Chicago Bulls next week at the United Center. That would mean he'd missed five total games. Mobley has averaged 16.9 points and 7.3 rebounds per game this season, his sixth in the league. The 25-year-old is in the second year of a five-year, $269 million deal with the Cavaliers, who selected him with the No. 3 overall pick back in 2021 out of USC. The Cavaliers will enter Monday night's matchup with the Bulls with a 7-7 record.

stories.title: Jordan Walsh continues to play himself into Boston’s lineup
stories.summary: Walsh thinks of himself as the best defender, and embodies that confidence on the court
stories.detailText: BOSTON, MA - NOVEMBER 15: Jordan Walsh #27 of the Boston Celtics drives to the basket during the game against the Dallas Mavericks on November 15, 2026 at TD Garden in Boston, Massachusetts. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and/or using this Photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Brian Babineau/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images Going into Sunday’s game against the Dallas Mavericks, I saw what Joe Mazzulla had in store for the Boston Celtics starting lineup. It was nothing out of the ordinary, but I found myself questioning why Jordan Walsh was still a part of it. This was Walsh’s eight start of the season out of 13 games, tied with Neemias Queta for the fourth most starts this season. The two of them trail only Jayson Tatum, Paul George, and Derrick White, the obvious core of the team. Clearly, Mazzulla sees something in Jordan. Why else would he continue to trust him night in, and night out? In Sunday’s rout of the Mavericks, a 131-94 victory for the Celtics, Walsh showed exactly how he earned the trust of his coach. He’s not going to be a big box score guy on a nightly basis, but he will still make his presence felt through grit, hard-nosed defense, and a whole lot of hustle. Boston took a historic lead against Dallas in the first quarter, ending the period up 42 to 9, the second-largest first quarter scoring differential in NBA history. Jordan had his fingerprints all over the game as the Celtics built their lead. From the jump, Boston’s defense was hounding the Mavericks, with Jordan Walsh being at the center of several possessions. Though the Celtics defense relies on plenty of switching, Jordan mostly found himself picking up Cooper Flagg and Naji Marshall, the two primary ball-handlers for Dallas. Walsh’s matchups weren’t bold enough to take a single field goal attempt in the quarter while he was the primary defender. Not only that, but Jordan was able to force two turnovers. He picked off a Marshall pass for Flagg which he took back for a tough transition bucket with a foul on one possession, and drew an illegal screen from Daniel Gafford not long after. In addition to his on-ball defense, Walsh was incredibly active off the ball, stunting drives and showing his hands to disrupt the Mavericks possessions while giving his teammates an extra second to get back in step with their matchups. When Jordan ultimately went to the bench for the first time, Boston held a 22-4 lead. All four of Dallas’s points came at the freethrow line. Meanwhile, Walsh was responsible for eight of Boston’s 22 points, tying his career-high for most points in the first quarter. Jordan Walsh is on the brink of losing minutes/his starting spot every game and he plays like it. Hard to take minutes away from a player like that pic.twitter.com/aICwWSL2w0 — Role Player Performances (@BenchHighlights) November 15, 2026 All of that being said, Jordan is far from a finished product. What he does have is an unbreakable spirit, and a desire to improve. He’s still a few months away from turning 23 years old, so even though it feels like he’s been around for a while, there’s plenty of untapped potential in there which we can see shine through on nights like this. Walsh made a rare podium appearance after the game, and provided us with some insight into how he views his role at this point. He explained how his value isn’t defined by the box score, saying “it’s never really about shots and points. It’s about ‘what can I create for the team?’ Can I create a situation where they can’t help off me? Can I create a situation where Cooper Flagg isn’t bringing the ball up the court and it’s somebody else? That’s how I find my way into the game.” When asked about his confidence as a defender he said “I think I’m the best defender. Every game is guarding the best player, and obviously the team, the organization believes I can do that every night so that’s why they put me on that guy. That in and of itself gives me the confidence to go out there and try to do the best I can.” Mazzulla gave some encouraging words to compliment that sentiment as well, saying “I think Jodan’s continuing to develop the mindset that we need him to have versus great players. And a great team has to have a group of guys that they can rely on to make it difficult for the team’s best player every single day… Jordan’s on that list.” Walsh even got a shoutout from Tatum in the press room, who added that Jordan, along with Baylor Scheierman, Hugo Gonzalez, and Ron Harper Jr., is more than capable in the starting spot. “Whether it’s on the defensive end, or knocking down shots, or crashing, those guys have been really, really good.” Clearly, the team is behind Walsh, and believes in his ability to contribute to the team. Don’t be surprised while we continue to see him in the starting lineup, or even when he has a big night off the bench.

stories.title: Las Vegas expansion focus turns to new arena (which could be new Summer League home)
stories.summary: All three groups in the final bidding are looking to build new arenas, with ambitious plans.
stories.detailText: In the coming weeks (maybe), the NBA is expected to choose between three groups looking to own and run a new franchise in Las Vegas. While the biggest factor in the winning bid will always be the money — with bids expected to be at or above $10 billion — another topic has come to the forefront: A new arena in Las Vegas. Specifically, one of the groups trying to win the bid — Golden Knights owner Bill Foley and former Suns owner Jerry Colangelo — has big plans for a new arena, which they detailed to Mike Vorkunov and Joe Vardon of The Athletic . Foley's group reached out to USA Basketball and the NBA Summer League to discuss its interest in hosting them in a possible new arena if the group were to win the bid for a new Vegas franchise, according to multiple league sources briefed on the pitch. There are two parts to that. As noted in the original report, USA Basketball is not moving its headquarters from Colorado Springs to Las Vegas. That said, the USA Men's National Team often starts its Olympics/World Cup training camps in Las Vegas, using UNLV's facilities and playing an exhibition game in the city. A new arena with top-flight facilities could be a draw for that kind of situation for USA teams. The NBA Summer League is also held annually on the UNLV campus, with games played in the Thomas & Mack Arena and the Cox Pavilion, which are connected by a shared lobby (allowing Summer League to have two games going at once that fans can bounce between). Warren LeGarie, who runs the Summer League, told The Athletic he would be open to a new venue if it met the league's needs. In the coming weeks, and certainly by the end of the year (per NBA Commissioner Adam Silver's previous comments), the league is expected to pick one of the three potential ownership groups in Las Vegas: Foley and Colangelo; Nancy Walton Laurie and her husband, Bill Laurie, with Lauri being a Walmart heir and Bill having owned the St. Louis Blues; former Bucks owner Marc Lasry, former Turner Broadcasting president David Levy and Canadian billionaire Steve Apostolopoulos. All three potential ownership groups have talked about a new arena, potentially as an anchor for a resort/casino complex and entertainment district. Exactly where this new arena and resort would go is undecided, which is part of the delay. Dallas Mavericks governor Patrick Dumont — the CEO and chairman of Las Vegas Sands — led part of the discussion around the Las Vegas team at the Board of Governors' meeting before the season. Getting a new arena designed, approved and built takes time and could mean the Las Vegas team will not tip off until the 2029-30 season. While Las Vegas has the 10-year-old T-Mobile Arena just off the Strip — home to the NHL's Golden Knights, the WNBA's Aces, and where the NBA has hosted the final rounds of the midseason NBA Cup the past two years — it would need up to $400 million in renovations to host an NBA team, Silver has said. While not off the table, that is less likely than building a new arena.

(Photo by Chris Coduto/Getty Images) | Getty Images Who : Phoenix Suns (5-7) @ Denver Nuggets (7-4) When : 7:00 pm Arizona Time Where : Ball Arena — Denver, Colorado Watch : Suns+, 3TV/AZFS Listen : KMVP 98.7 Following a seven-game homestand, the Phoenix Suns hit the road for a three-game stint that begins on the second night of a back-to-back in the Mile High City. They’ll take on a Denver Nuggets squad that already defeated them 127-120 earlier this season. And while the Nuggets haven’t necessarily looked like the world beaters we’ve grown accustomed to seeing in recent years, they possess enough foundational continuity to remain a formidable opponent. Meanwhile, the Phoenix Suns continue to search for answers surrounding a starting five that has struggled to establish any semblance of efficiency, cohesion, or stability through the first 12 games of the season. The bench has routinely kept Phoenix competitive and, in large part, is the reason the Suns have five victories to their name. Perhaps getting away from home will do this group some good. For a basketball team still searching for its identity, maybe the process of finding itself begins on the road in Denver. Tale of the Tape Probable Starters Injury Report Suns Mark Williams — OUT (Left Shoulder Surgery) Ryan Dunn — QUESTIONABLE (Right Thumb Soreness) Nuggets Julian Strawther — OUT (Left Knee Sprain) What to Watch For There have been two constants for the Phoenix Suns this season. The starting unit has been horrendous, and the rebounding has followed suit. So once again, what we’ll be watching for tonight is whether that starting five can demonstrate any semblance of connectivity on the offensive end while possessing the ability to get stops defensively. It’s a dangerous combination right now. The starting unit struggles to generate efficient offense and has been equally ineffective at preventing opponents from doing so. Its most productive stretches typically coincide with Devin Booker putting the team on his back, and there’s very little consistency in the production surrounding him. That’s an unsustainable formula for success, particularly against quality opponents. That’s where my primary focus will be tonight. What can the Suns’ starting five accomplish collectively on both ends of the floor? Can they establish an offensive rhythm that doesn’t require Booker to shoulder the entire burden? Can they disrupt Denver’s offense and finish defensive possessions by securing rebounds? It would be nice to see the starting five establish the tone of a basketball game for once, rather than asking the second unit to come in and change it. Key to a Suns Win While the Suns rank 30th in the NBA in rebounds per game, the Nuggets rank 23rd, so rebounding might not be the primary determining factor in tonight’s outcome, although it should always be an area of emphasis for Phoenix given its struggles this season. The key to success tonight is taking care of the basketball. The Nuggets rank seventh in the NBA in steals per game, making them a pesky, feisty defensive team capable of generating extra possessions by forcing turnovers. Fortunately, one thing the Suns have done well this season is exercising discipline with the basketball, committing the sixth fewest turnovers per game in the league. That trend needs to continue tonight in Denver. The Suns already surrender enough extra possessions through their inability to rebound. There’s no need to gift their opponent additional opportunities by being careless with the basketball. Prediction The remainder of this road trip presents some favorable matchups for Phoenix, but traveling to Denver on the second night of a back-to-back is a tough ask. Granted, the starters didn’t play at all in the fourth quarter against the Lakers because the bench was busy carrying the load. Can the starters return the favor tonight and give the second unit an opportunity to get some rest in their legs? Given what we’ve witnessed through the first 12 games of the season, I don’t see it happening tonight. Nuggets 118, Suns 109

stories.title: JJ Redick puts Lakers ‘trend’ on blast despite 8th straight win
stories.summary: The Lakers have shown a troubling trend through the season's first month.
stories.detailText: PHOENIX — The Lakers’ eighth straight win didn’t stop coach J.J. Redick from getting real about one of the team’s troubling trends. The Lakers’ victory over the Suns on Sunday played out similarly to other wins they’ve had this season: An explosive first quarter from Luka Dončić leading to the Lakers having an advantage and a double-digit lead going into halftime before a dominant third quarter gives them a comfortable lead. Los Angeles Lakers head coach J.J. Redick, center, isn’t happy with how his team has handled big leads late in games. AP Photo/Darryl Webb And then they let go of the rope before pulling out a victory after nearly blowing a significant lead, which is exactly what happened when the Suns cut the Lakers’ 31-point lead in the third quarter to five in the fourth before the Lakers won the game by eight. “I told the team this after the game: We’re working too hard and we’re playing too hard to build these leads,” Redick said. “It’s a disservice to each other to take your foot off the gas.” Sunday wasn’t an anomaly, either. The Lakers are one of the league’s worst fourth quarter teams. AP Photo/Aaron Gash The Lakers, who are tied for the league’s best record at 12-2, have the league’s second-best net rating in first quarters (plus-18.7), sixth-best rating in second quarters (plus-12.5) and best net rating in third quarters (plus-24.5). But they have the second-worst net rating in fourth quarters (minus-24.4) because their defense falls off a cliff, leading to them blowing big leads . The Lakers’ 131.3 defensive rating in fourth quarters is the league’s second-worst mark. Los Angeles Lakers forward Ziaire Williams (11), Luka Doncic (77), Jake LaRavia (12) and Walker Kessler (14) wait during a timeout against the Phoenix Suns, Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in Phoenix. AP Photo/Darryl Webb The Lakers left Phoenix with the win despite nearly blowing a 31-point lead. Getty Images “You have to play for 48 minutes and we’re going to need our defense to win us games,” Redick said. “ These guys want to be a top-10 defense , we think we can be a good defensive team, I believe we can be a good defensive team. This has been consistent now, this is a trend. Gotta be better in the fourth quarter.” The Lakers will tie their longest winning streak under Redick if they beat the Hornets on Tuesday. But the former NBA sharpshooter isn’t allowing his team’s current success to distract from the areas they need to improve at.

stories.title: Warriors rookie takes dramatic step in the barbershop; earns eye-popping comparison
stories.summary: You know the saying: Look good, feel good. Well, Yaxel Lendeborg apparently subscribes to the inverse philosophy.
stories.detailText: NEW ORLEANS — You know the saying: Look good, feel good. Well, Yaxel Lendeborg apparently subscribes to the inverse philosophy. The bold and brash Warriors rookie slogged through the worst game of his young career the last time he took the court. He went 1-for-13 from the field and the Warriors, in their first game without Steph Curry , were handed nearly a 50-point loss by the red-hot Spurs. Yaxel Lendeborg #1 of the Golden State Warriors and Stephon Castle #5 of the San Antonio Spurs play during the NBA Cup in San Antonio, Nov. 13, 2026. NBAE via Getty Images He felt awful. So he changed his look. “He actually told me before he took his hood off and showed me his haircut,” Golden State forward Georges Niang said. Or else, he may not have even recognized the rookie. “Ain’t nothing wrong with a low Caesar, man. He looks professional.” Lendeborg was so distraught over the loss that he needed a new hairdo that showed he meant business. Mission accomplished. Somewhere on a barbershop floor here in the Big Easy is the big hair that Lendeborg once embodied. “He chopped all his hair off. You’ll see,” coach Steve Kerr said. “I didn’t even recognize him. Apparently that’s his response to getting beat by a hundred – to go right to the barber.” Yaxel Lendeborg of the Golden State Warriors arrives at the Frost Bank Center before a game against the San Antonio Spurs in San Antonio, Friday, Nov. 13, 2026. NBAE via Getty Images It wasn’t quite a hundred, but it felt like it to Lendeborg, who used the same terminology in his customarily honest comments after the loss. After all, on his run to a national championship last season with Michigan, the Wolverines lost three games — by a combined 16 points. “We just lost by like 100,” Lendeborg said Saturday night. “So you know I’m f—ed up mentally right now. … I was flustered the entire game. Couldn’t make a damn layup.” Kerr saw the comments after the game and used Lendeborg to make a point to the rest of the team when they regrouped for practice Sunday at Tulane University’s gym. “I loved how honest he is, how vulnerable he is. There’s no pretense. He’s just telling you exactly how he feels,” Kerr said. “Our message today was how you respond.” Even in his short NBA career, Lendeborg hasn’t had many tough nights personally. Over his first 12 games before Saturday night, he had scored in double figures 11 times, averaging 21.7. Yaxel Lendeborg of the Golden State Warriors ties his shoes during a game against the San Antonio Spurs in San Antonio, Friday, Nov. 13, 2026. NBAE via Getty Images Lendeborg and the Warriors get their first chance to put the blowout behind them Monday night in New Orleans against a Pelicans team they beat by 51 last week. Of course, that was with a healthy Curry and the Warriors rolling amid an eight-game winning streak. Without Curry, who will miss at least the next two weeks with a tear in his oblique, the Warriors’ fate largely hinges on Lendeborg’s ability to move on from his bad game. “I’m excited for Yaxel,” Niang said before tipoff. “He has raw emotion, which is great. It’s like the purity of what’s going on. Yaxel’s just gonna say how he actually feels. And you’re like, Oh, well I do feel that. Maybe I don’t say it. But that’s the best thing about him.” Niang, a veteran in his 10th season playing for his sixth different team, has shared a locker room with lots of different personalities. To find a comparison for Lendeborg, though, he had to go across sports — to the gridiron. “I don’t know if you find that [honesty] from any other player in the league of his stature,” Niang said. “I’m not gonna do him a disservice and put these two in the same category, but you think about someone in football who’s raw with his emotions, like Jameis Winston, right? “Yaxel’s probably a little more serious than some of the stuff you get from Jameis Winston, no disrespect, but that raw emotion is awesome to see.” Golden State Warriors player Yaxel Lendeborg looks on during a game against the San Antonio Spurs in San Antonio, Texas, Friday, Nov. 13, 2026. NBAE via Getty Images Niang reminded Lendeborg that it was just one game of 82, and in November, without Curry, to boot. But, he said, “I think he likes to feel his emotions and kind of go through it.” Everyone processes losses differently. Kerr, a five-time champion as a player, joked that it took him until the final of his 15 seasons before he was able to “My last year I was finally fine,” he said. “My first 14 years I was a mess. I’m kind of kidding. It’s one of the hardest things to do when you’re a competitor — to get over a bad loss and a bad personal game. … It’s not necessarily learning how to lose; it’s about learning how to respond to a loss.”

(Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) | Getty Images After exiting Wednesday’s win over the Milwaukee Bucks midway through the third quarter, Los Angeles Lakers star Austin Reaves missed Sunday’s victory against the Phoenix Suns with a bruised heel. Two days prior, head coach JJ Redick spoke with reporters and said Reaves is day-to-day while considering the injury to be minor. Prior to the game Sunday, Redick provided an update on Reaves. “He’s improving. Again, it really comes down to just like a pain tolerance thing,” Redick said. “Nothing structural beyond a bruise. I think every day it’s been better and we’ll see where he’s at in 48 hours when we play on Tuesday.” While it’s far from set in stone, it sounds like Reaves has a chance to play Tuesday against the Charlotte Hornets. Although he was ruled out on Saturday for the Suns game, Redick didn’t declare him out when he talked with the media on Friday, so it seems as though this is a game-to-game injury, at worst. That’s an encouraging prognosis and suggests Reaves will be back in the lineup before too long. The Lakers play again Wednesday against the Utah Jazz for the second half of a back-to-back set, so it’s possible Reaves would only suit up for one of those games regardless, if he’s even ready to go. He missed the second leg of Los Angeles’ back-to-back last week against the Atlanta Hawks, too, so caution may be the guiding principle here. In Reaves’ absence Sunday evening, Luka Dončić continued his dazzling play behind 43 points — including 20 in the first quarter — and nine assists while Quentin Grimes rejoined the squad after missing the previous two games with a finger injury and added 22 points on 7-of-10 shooting (5-of-6 beyond the arc). Collin Sexton notched 16 points on 6-of-11 shooting to extend his own recent stretch of strong play, too. Of course, the Lakers are at their best with Reaves available, so they’ll hope he’s back as soon as possible and it’s a positive development that he’s merely navigating a pain tolerance dynamic rather than any serious issues. The Lakers and Hornets face off at 8 p.m. Tuesday night. You can follow Jackson on Twitter at @jackfrank_jjf .

Queta, the Celtics’ starting center for most of the season, is listed as questionable with rest. He has yet to miss a game this season, though the Celtics have rested Jayson Tatum, Paul George, and Mitchell Robinson for one game each. Joe Mazzulla spoke glowingly about Queta after Sunday’s game. “I feel like his growth and his role has gone kind of under the radar,” Mazzulla said. “He’s more important than just for defense. He’s important in the locker room. He’s important on the offensive end. He just continues to get better and better. It’s easy to overlook it because of how easy he kind of makes it sometimes. And you can feel it when he’s not — a couple times he’s not playing well, it’s so noticeable because of how good he is.” “He’s just a guy that I have a lot of joy watching because of who he was when he got here and who he is now. And everybody wants to become the player that you have to rely on. And he’s been that for us.” Queta is averaging 9.1 points and 6.6 rebounds this season, while shooting 57.3% from the field. He’s also made 4 of his 5 three-point attempts this season as he continues to expand his game. Mitchell Robinson could return to the starting lineup If Queta sits, Mitchell Robinson, who started the Celtics’ first five games of the season, could slide back into the starting lineup, with Luka Garza is available as well. Robinson is averaging 5.2 points and 5.5 rebounds per game in 17.7 minutes off the bench. The Celtics have managed their centers on back-to-backs before this season. Robinson sat on the front end of the team’s first back-to-back in Orlando on November 1st, and Queta started in his place. Queta has started every game since. The Celtics are on the second night of a back-to-back after blowing out the Dallas Mavericks 131-94 on Sunday night at TD Garden. Boston outscored Dallas 42-9 in the first quarter, the largest first-quarter point differential in franchise history. Jayson Tatum was the only Celtic to play more than 25 minutes on Sunday; he erupted for 32 points, 6 assists, and 6 rebounds in 30 minutes. “We got a really, really good team,” Tatum said after. “And I think it really just starts with our depth.” Jayson Tatum said tonight the Celtics have a “really good” team Asked him when he realized that: “At some point in Charleston, it kind of clicked.” pic.twitter.com/QN7ulXxuEz — Noa Dalzell 🏀 (@NoaDalzell) November 16, 2026 The Celtics are 11-2, lead the Eastern Conference, and have won six straight games. The Magic have won three straight Orlando, who is 5-7 on the season, arrives in Boston riding a three-game winning streak, most recently a 107-99 win over the Milwaukee Bucks on Friday night. The Magic remain without Paolo Banchero, who is out with a right high ankle sprain. Jonathan Isaac (left knee injury management), Noah Penda (partially torn right hamstring), and Izaiyah Nelson (left ankle injury recovery) are also out. Jalen Suggs and Tristan da Silva have both returned from injuries and are off the injury report. Franz Wagner has carried the load without Banchero, averaging 24.4 points, 8.3 assists, and 6.8 rebounds per game. The Celtics beat the Magic 108-97 in Orlando on November 1st. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images We’ve reached the point where a “normal” performance from Victor Wembanyama is something like a 28-point double-double with four blocks. For the second time this season and fifth time in his career, Wemby has been named Western Conference Player of the Week. He joins Tim Duncan, David Robinson and Tony Parker as the only Spurs to win it five or more times. 𝗪𝗘𝗦𝗧𝗘𝗥𝗡 𝗖𝗢𝗡𝗙𝗘𝗥𝗘𝗡𝗖𝗘 𝗣𝗟𝗔𝗬𝗘𝗥 𝗢𝗙 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗪𝗘𝗘𝗞 👽 pic.twitter.com/d4TCmLGjUv — San Antonio Spurs (@spurs) November 16, 2026 Wemby’s biggest perforamnce of the week came in Phoenix, where he recorded 40 points, 11 rebounds and eight blocks — all in just 25 minutes of action — in a 122-96 win that even had the opposing crowd (one that is usually very anti-Spurs) cheering him on. He joined Wilt Chamberlain as the only the second player in NBA history to record multiple games in a season with at least 40 points, 10 rebounds and 8 blocks. He also had 32 points, 9 rebounds and 5 blocks in the Spurs come-from-behind 124-119 win against the Bulls. It was the Week of the Freaks, as he is joined by Giannis Antetokounmpo as Eastern Conference Player of the Week, who helped lead the Miami Heat to a 3-0 week while averaging 33.7 points, 11.3 rebounds, 4.7 assists, and 1.3 blocks.

teamStories.detailText: SAN ANTONIO, TX -NOVEMBER 13: Victor Wembanyama #1 of the San Antonio Spurs goes for a rebound against Golden State Warriors in the first half of a Emirates Cup game at Frost Bank Center on November 13, 2026 in San Antonio, Texas. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Ronald Cortes/Getty Images) | Getty Images I’m back with another update about the rest of the Western Conference. Just like last week, both the San Antonio Spurs and Los Angeles Lakers are on lengthy winning streak joyrides. The Spurs have won 12 straight while Los Angeles has won eight in a row . Anyhow, let’s get to it. Net ratings are courtesy of Cleaning the Glass and exclude garbage time. Playoff teams 1. San Antonio Spurs: 12-2, plus-15.2 net rating (1st in the NBA) Lakers’ record vs. Spurs: 0-0 Led by Victor Wembanyama and Dylan Harper, the Spurs have been absolutely dominant since an 0-2 start. They rank third in both offensive and defensive rating and are pummeling virtually every team they face. Their matchup with the Lakers on Nov. 27 could be quite illuminating for both sides. 2. Houston Rockets: 11-3, plus-12.1 (3rd) Lakers’ record vs. Rockets: 0-0 An undefeated 4-0 week helped Houston wash away the taste of a 2-3 stretch following its 5-0 start. After a three-week absence, Steven Adams returned to the lineup during the Rockets’ 147-119 rout of the Washington Wizards Sunday evening while Alperen Şengün dropped 43 points, 12 rebounds and five assists in a win over the Utah Jazz on Friday to continue his career-best campaign. 3. Portland Trail Blazers: 9-3, plus-7.0 (8th) Lakers’ record vs. Blazers: 1-1 The Blazers rebounded from back-to-back losses against the Spurs and Lakers to twice knock off the shorthanded Oklahoma City Thunder before scoring an easy road win over the Sacramento Kings. Damian Lillard’s shooting has really invigorated this group and he looks pretty dang good for a 36-year-old coming off a torn Achilles. it does appear that Damian Lillard would like you to know what time it is pic.twitter.com/NWTYE40cih — Steve Jones (@stevejones20) November 11, 2026 4. Minnesota Timberwolves: 9-4, plus-12.0 (3rd) Lakers’ record vs. Timberwolves: 0-0 The Timberwolves were en fuego before the Chicago Bulls surprisingly beat the brakes off them Saturday night. Still, they’ve done quite well without Anthony Edwards, largely thanks to LaMelo Ball, Rudy Gobert, Jaden McDaniels, Ayo Dosunmu and Jonathan Kuminga. They’ll be tested this week with a home back-to-back against the Blazers before welcoming the New York Knicks and Memphis Grizzlies to town. 5. Memphis Grizzlies: 9-4, plus-7.5 (6th) Lakers’ record vs. Grizzlies: 0-0 After losing three in a row, the Grizzlies have won three of their last four against an undermanned Toronto Raptors team and the lottery-bound New Orleans Pelicans and Brooklyn Nets. Wins are wins but we’ll get a better gauge of their quality this week when they face the Cleveland Cavaliers and Minnesota Timberwolves on the road. What I do know is Cedric Coward absolutely rules. Play-In teams 6. Oklahoma City Thunder: 9-5 (10th) Lakers’ record vs. Thunder: 0-0 The Thunder had a tough week, losing both ends of a road back-to-back against Portland before seeing Darius Garland dash their NBA Cup dreams with a game-winning and-one Friday night. They did snap their three-game skid Sunday with a tidy win over the Kings, though, as Shai Gilgeous-Alexander tallied 37 points on 13-of-20 shooting. Down three starters, including two All-Stars, Oklahoma City remains ravaged by injury and trying to stay afloat. 7. Denver Nuggets: 7-4, plus-1.8 (13th) Lakers’ record vs. Nuggets: 0-0 The Nuggets have oddly played a league-low 11 games thus far while other teams have already played 14. Regardless, they’ve looked a bit better since a 3-3 start and have won four of five. Nikola Jokić is gradually rounding into form and Jamal Murray has been sensational. Duels with the Rockets and Boston Celtics this week should challenge them. NIKOLA JOKIĆ AND JAMAL MURRAY MADE MAJOR HISTORY TONIGHT. They are the FIRST pair of teammates since tracking began in 1997-98 to record 1,000+ assists to each other 🤯 Jokić in DEN's W: 26p, 8r, 10a, 3s Murray in DEN's W: 23p, 7r, 9a, 2b pic.twitter.com/h0TxxKdcAl — NBA (@NBA) November 15, 2026 8. Golden State Warriors: 8-5, plus-3.2 (11th) Lakers’ record vs. Warriors: 1-1 How quickly circumstances change in the NBA. The Warriors had won eight in a row entering Wednesday’s showdown with Houston. Then, Stephen Curry exited early because of injury . He’s expected to miss around one month with an oblique abdominal tear, according to ESPN’s Shams Charania. Golden State dropped a close one to Houston Wednesday then was a dead man walking against the Spurs on Friday and lost by 38. They’ll hope to shift the vibes Monday night against New Orleans. 9. Dallas Mavericks: 7-7, minus-3.6 (20th) Lakers’ record vs. Mavericks: 0-0 Speaking of circumstances changing quickly, hello, Dallas Mavericks. Last week, I heaped praise upon Cooper Flagg and the new-look Mavs. Now, they’ve lost three straight games by a combined 86 points — including one to the second-string Cleveland Cavaliers — and Flagg’s shot 16-of-46 from the floor over that span. Woof. Lottery teams 10. Phoenix Suns: 5-7, minus-5.6 (23rd) Lakers’ record vs. Suns: 1-0 The Suns are just a bit of a jumbled mess. They rarely seem competitive against fellow playoff hopefuls, are severely undersized defensively and often find themselves in rotation with no way to counteract it. Devin Booker is scoring the heck out of the ball, however, averaging 24.8 points on 60.9% true shooting. DEVIN BOOKER DOWN THE STRETCH 🔥 3 OF HIS 30 POINTS. BACK-TO-BACK Ws FOR PHX! pic.twitter.com/uVSCrrWua2 — NBA (@NBA) November 13, 2026 11. Los Angeles Clippers: 4-8, minus-4.2 (21st) Lakers’ record vs. Clippers: 2-0 Following a 1-7 start, the Clippers have established a bit of traction with three wins in four tries. They’ll look to push their winning streak to three games Tuesday night against the Jazz. 12. New Orleans Pelicans: 4-10, minus-8.2 (25th) Lakers’ record vs. Pelicans: 0-0 The good vibes of a four-game winning streak are a total relic now. New Orleans has lost six straight and Dejounte Murray recently requested a trade. The Pelicans are in a disarray and play such sticky, incongruent basketball because of a funky roster makeup. 13. Sacramento Kings: 1-2, minus-12.8 (29th) Lakers’ record vs. Kings: 1-0 The Kings are winless at home and rarely even keep games close. But rookie guard Darius Acuff Jr. is a legitimate bright spot, and I’m intrigued by Dylan Cardwell’s bouncy, energy-infused skill-set. He and Maxime Raynaud could be a fun front-court pairing whenever Raynaud returns from injury. DARIUS ACUFF JR. MADE HISTORY LAST NIGHT 👏 32 PTS 10 AST 5 REB 3 3PM He joined LeBron James (3x) as the only teenagers in NBA history to record 30+ points and 10+ assists in multiple games 👑 pic.twitter.com/aoMv5noYVd — NBA (@NBA) November 9, 2026 14. Utah Jazz: 1-13, minus-11.3 (27th) Lakers’ record vs. Jazz: 1-0 The Jazz are bad and injured. It’s a terrible place to be. The absences of Jaren Jackson Jr., Lauri Markkanen and Jusuf Nurkić leave them incredibly depleted up front. They do not get to the rim, are a poor, low-volume outside shooting team and rarely tilt defenses with their passing. It’s a tough recipe. Darryn Peterson does seem to be finding his stride, though, and that’s among the most crucial storylines for Utah this season. You can follow Jackson on Twitter at @jackfrank_jjf .

teamStories.detailText: SALT LAKE CITY, UT - NOVEMBER 15: Dylan Harper #2, Keldon Johnson #3, Stephon Castle #5, and Luke Kornet #7 of the San Antonio Spurs look on during the game against the Utah Jazz on November 15, 2026 at Delta Center in Salt Lake City, Utah. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this Photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Melissa Majchrzak/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images Welcome to Week in Review: a Monday feature that looks back at the week that was for the San Antonio Spurs , takes a look at the week ahead, and more. Enjoy! Week 3 : The Spurs extended their winning streak to 8 with three blowout wins — two expected ones at home against the Jazz and in Sacramento, plus a somewhat surprising one at Portland — sandwiched around an all-time classic against the Mavericks. The Spurs got out to a 19-point lead before blowing it in all-too-familiar fashion, but Victor Wembanyama channeled his inner Wilt Chamberlain to help gut out the one-point win with a historic 53-point, 24-rebound, 8-block effort. Week 4: 4-0 (12-2, 1st in West ) 112-96 win at Phoenix Suns Battling off some demons in what is often a challenging venue, the Spurs went into Phoenix and demoralized another middling opponent trying to find its footing. They countered a 32-point outing from Devin Booker with 40-11-8 showing from Wemby, who even had Suns fans cheering after it became clear that the Spurs had this one in the bag, and they decided to just enjoy the show. 124-119 win at Chicago Bulls It wasn’t their prettiest showing, but the Spurs weathered an insanely hot start from the Bulls — who at one point in the second quarter were shooting 83% from both the field and three — before bouncing back and with a dominant second half to overcome a 22-point deficit for their 10th straight win. 123-85 win vs. Golden State Warriors (NBA Emirates Cup) An anticipated match-up lost its luster after vintage Steph Curry was ruled out with an oblique tear, but the Spurs didn’t let that get in their way. Motivated by being home after a four-game road trip, they put on a show for their home crowd by starting on a franchise-record 18-0 run and never looked back. Stephon Castle finally broke out of his offensive slump with 32 points and 6 assist. The Warriors were so demoralized that Draymond Green went back to his shtick of trying (but somehow failing) to get himself ejected , and Rookie of the Year candidate Yaxel Lendeborg admitted to being so “f***ed up mentally” after the game that he… cut his hair ? (I get it after a series of bad games — Wemby and Keldon Johnson did it last January — but one game?) 110-102 win at Utah Jazz This one had all the hallmarks of a trap game, and it almost worked: right back out on the road, altitude, Sunday matinee, 11-game winning streak vs. 11-game losing streak, and an opponent so shorthanded they have nothing to lose. For the second time this season, the Spurs went into Utah and had to work for the win. Mo Bamba gave them the Curry performance they missed the game before by going 6-6 from three (his first six attempts of the season!), but again, the Spurs weathered the storm and countered with a career-high 31 points from Dylan Harper. As weird as it is to say about a 1-13 team that they swept, I’m glad the Spurs are done with the Jazz for this season. Power Rankings John Schuhmann, NBA.com — 1 (last week: 1) OffRtg: 119.2 (3) DefRtg: 106.6 (3) NetRtg: +12.6 (2) The Spurs were down 22 points in Chicago on Wednesday, and they trailed by three with a little more than three minutes left in Utah over the weekend. But their winning streak is now at 12 games , and they remain at the top of the Western Conference. Two takeaways Victor Wembanyama played just 25 minutes in Phoenix last Monday. But in those 25 minutes, he had 40 points, 11 rebounds and eight blocks. With another 12 blocks (and only four fouls) over the last three games, he has 2.3 times as many blocks ( 60 ) as fouls (26), which would easily be the highest ratio for a player with at least 50 blocks in the 54 seasons that they’ve been counted, topping his own mark of 1.7 blocks per foul two seasons ago. According to Synergy tracking, the Spurs now lead the league in both transition points per game ( 29.4 ) and transition points allowed per game ( 16.4 ). Over their last five games, they’ve outscored their opponents by 116 points (155-39) in transition. Coming up: One other team ranks in the top six in both transition points and transition points allowed per game, and it’s the Pistons, who the Spurs will host on Tuesday. After that, they’ll face three teams – the Clippers, Pelicans and Kings – in the bottom four in the West. Law Murray, The Athletic — 1 (last week: 1) Make that three straight weeks of wins for the defending Western Conference champions. Harris, San Antonio’s top offseason acquisition, still hasn’t debuted. But the Spurs are the only team in the league that is top three on both offense and defense, and they won games with Devin Vassell and De’Aaron Fox missing at least one start apiece. Kurt Helin, NBC Sports — 1 (last week: 2) San Antonio has a net rating of +12.6, just off Oklahoma City’s historic rating (+12.7) in 2024-25 season, when the Thunder won 68 games and the NBA title. The Spurs are looking to become the first team to lose in the NBA Finals and then return to that big stage since the Cavaliers in 2018 — and they are off to a fast start. San Antonio has a top-three offensive and defensive rating. A lot of that has been because of Victor Wembanyama’s impressive start to the season, but the guard lineups — with De’Aaron Fox, Dylan Harper, Stephon Castle and Devin Vassell, in whatever combination — are thriving as well. Check them out for yourselves Tuesday night on Coast 2 Coast on NBC and Peacock , starting at 8 ET. Brett Siegel, Clutch Points — 1 (last week: 2) Four of the Spurs’ last five wins have come by at least 15 points. The only single-digit wins in this span were against the Chicago Bulls and Utah Jazz. In that game against the Bulls, San Antonio trailed by 22 points before outscoring the Bulls 68-49 in the second half. The Spurs have now won 12 straight games since losing back-to-back games to begin the 2026-27 season. Each of the last three times the Spurs won at least 12 straight games, they went on to win at least 61 games. San Antonio ranks inside the top 3 in both offensive and defensive rating. Coming up Tues. 11/17 vs. Detroit Pistons (7:00 PM CT) Thurs. 11/19 vs. Los Angeles Clippers (7:00 PM CT) Sat. 11/21 vs. New Orleans Pelicans (7:00 PM CT) Prediction: 3-0 — After playing five of their last six games on the road, the Spurs finally get to stay home all week for what feels like an extended homestand (at least by this season’s standards). They’re still in search of their first “signature” win of the season and look like they could use a challenge, and Tuesday’s match-up against the Pistons may provide just that (although, like the Portland and Golden State games, it’s tainted by no Jalen Duren). After that, the Clippers and Pelicans shouldn’t present much of a challenge and may not even provide them with a chance to go up against two disgruntled former Spurs, with Kawhi Leonard hightailing it back to Toronto and Dejounte Murray possibly sitting out after demanding a trade. (I get the feeling Pop’s fatherly love for these two shielded them from a lot of bad press in SA.)
