teamStories.detailText: SALT LAKE CITY, UTAH - NOVEMBER 15: Mo Bamba #44 of the Utah Jazz grabs a rebound against Stephon Castle #5 and Keldon Johnson #3 of the San Antonio Spurs during the first half of their game at the Delta Center on November 15, 2026 in Salt Lake City, Utah. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement.(Photo by Chris Gardner/ Getty Images) | Getty Images Those of us who have been roaming the beat of hyper-focused amateur basketball blogging for long enough know that, at any given moment, we are prone to spouting off the odd exaggeration or two. An embellishment, if you will. Saying something as innocuous as “that’s one of the coolest plays I’ve ever seen” is a part of the set decoration around here and, if I could take you behind the curtain even further, I’d venture to say that unsheathing our hyperbolic sword to wax poetic about the tragedies and triumphs of regular old basketball moments is actually the whole gig. It’s our mandate from heaven. From the mundane, we must divine the remarkable. Now, taking that rather large grain of salt and tucking it away in your subconscious, I invite you to entertain the idea that the 1st quarter of basketball the Spurs played against the Warriors on Friday night was maybe the greatest 12 minutes of basketball I’ve seen this group play. Ever? I mean, who has the time to research forever, but for the sake of this conversation, let’s say, yeah, that was the best stretch I’ve ever seen. Everything worked. They opened the game on an 18-0 run and the quarter ended 38-14. The offense seemed to flow in and out of infinite possibilities at random. A three, a dunk, a layup, a middie. The basket glowed in a shining iridescence of joy and wonder at the possibilities before it. The defense, on the other hand, appeared to absorb the deep grey of the NBA Cup court and became a void into which offense flattened out into a shadow of itself. The Warriors, 5-for-25 in the quarter, were swallowed up in this cloud, shrinking and disappearing into nothingness while our silver-clad demons continued to gleefully romp through this realm of dreams and nightmares. That quarter was so insane that I’m still sitting here thinking about it four days later. In fact, as I watched that very same group of basketball gods look exceedingly mortal out there in Utah yesterday afternoon, the vividness of their display against the Warriors only became more stark in comparison. As inevitable as the Spurs seemed the other night, the letdown was equally so. Sunday afternoon was a slog. An uphill battle against a team desperate to find a foothold in this season. You could feel the wild energy radiating off the Jazz the entire game. A burbling, untethered sort of raw power that seemed equally likely to hit the target or harm innocent bystanders. Mo Bamba went 6-for-6 from three and 0-for-3 at the line. There was nothing precise or controlled about their approach; instead, they seemed animated by an unseen force trying to make something, anything, out of what is rapidly becoming a lost season. Into this tempest rode the good ship Spurs, and immediately the goal was to weather it. Survive and endure. Perfection is not something that can be found in a storm, and so they abandoned it. Everything became less fluid and more practical. They held back, they picked their spots, and they took the opportunities provided to them. Even as the Jazz surged ahead again and again, the Spurs calmly stayed the course. They applied the pressure slowly and deliberately until the end when, their opponent’s frenzied blows finally slowing, they steadily pushed through and saw it out. No real theatrics. No otherworldly displays. Just a group playing with a sort of dogged determination and certainty that, in the end, their process would take them where they needed to go. The contrast of these two performances is fascinating to observe side by side, although, as we’ve discussed ad nauseam, it’s hard to know exactly how much, if any, of this translates toward the ultimate goal of redemption at the end of the season. The Warriors were without Curry. The Jazz were without hope. Every team the Spurs face has some sort of flaw or hindrance that keeps them from revealing the true nature of these Spurs, and so we are left to our own devices. Forced to spend the next few months reading tea leaves and trying to understand what exactly these guys might be capable of. The idea that the Spurs have the ability to touch perfection, to wield it, if only for a moment, is a tantalizing one. It’s an exciting new dimension to their ceiling, and the thought of them unleashing it in a playoff atmosphere sends chills down my spine. You can conjure that vision in your mind, can’t you? The crowd feeding off it. The sounds growing louder. The players bouncing and vibrating off each other in a kind of combustion designed to obliterate their opponent from the face of the earth. Somewhere in there, the light goes strange and your voice drops an octave. We would be conquerors. We would be kings. We would be gods, beautiful and terrible as the Dawn! But we’ve seen how that goes in the playoffs, haven’t we? We’ve seen this group in their bag against elite competition and we’ve seen how quickly that high can dissipate until all of a sudden there’s a vacuum. It’s cold and dark when that power deserts you and, in that void, you can lose track of how you climbed that mountain in the first place. These Spurs didn’t have an answer last June when they reached for divine inspiration and came up empty. They became shells of themselves and watched as the tide washed over them, extinguishing what was left of their dream. As Stephon Castle casually loped down the court before throwing down a nonchalant windmill dunk to officially put this game to bed yesterday, I felt a profound satisfaction come over me. In the 4th quarter, they calmly erased the Jazz’s 5-point lead. Dylan Harper, quietly and competently, poured in 18. Victor controlled the paint, Steph, Devin and Keldon repeatedly took advantage of Utah’s desperation, and before you knew it the game was over. It was always over. It was over before it started. It wasn’t the greatest 12 minutes of basketball I’ve seen this group play, but, in a way, that was even more impressive. Takeaways Sure, so I maybe downplayed the extent to which Dylan Harper’s 4th quarter was amazing up there because it fit the narrative I was trying to sell. So sue me! The hyperbole sword cuts both ways! But that was main body Charlie, and we’re in Takeaway land now, where we’re free to say whatever the hell we want about Harper’s 4th quarter takeover. It’s telling that the Spurs don’t need him to become an apex predator all the time, but it’s a remarkable card that they get to play in certain spots. The Spurs had spent the night being mildly competent, getting mostly the same looks they’re used to and simply not executing. Shots weren’t falling. Passes were slightly off, cuts were a step slow. The beautiful game wasn’t so beautiful at the moment, and what it needed was a tool to cut through the red tape. Harper turned into a machete. He looked fast, thorough, and sharp as a tack. Put simply, he just relentlessly looked like the best player on the court. It was a career high in points for him, a record that I’m sure will be fleeting. What a player. I’m almost sad that the Spurs relative competence erased the 6 of 6 miracle night from Mo Bama. Genuinely incredible thing to witness. The Luke Kornet situation is so fascinating. The effect of having Wembanyama around makes everything else really difficult to contextualize. Is Kornet bad at basketball, or is he just normal and the dropoff from Vic’s insanity so steep that it makes you feel like you’re getting the rug pulled out from under you? You can even see it with our guys. They’re out there throwing weird, very Wemby-coded lob passes to this poor guy who’s just trying to crash the basket, and he looks silly when the ball glances off his hands or the backboard or whatever. Meanwhile we’re all sitting there like, “Geez, we gotta figure out this backup center situation.” But I truly don’t know what there is to be done. Vic can’t play 48 minutes. Whoever comes in is never going to be him. I can feel the walls closing in a little bit on Keldon Johnson’s time as a Spur. Maybe it won’t be this year, but it feels like something eventually might have to give where we can’t afford to pay him we he deserves to get paid. I dunno. I’m trying not to think about it and I’m hoping I’m wrong. I’m so glad he has a mustache this year. KJ hit 'em with the hook 👀 📺 @DAZN pic.twitter.com/4xYQZV4AXO — San Antonio Spurs (@spurs) November 15, 2026 WWL Post Game Press Conference Aren’t mustaches sort of played out at this point? Played out? Yeah, like, weren’t we doing ironic mustaches in the hipster community around 2009? People were tattooing little mustaches on their finger as a bit? You don’t think we’ve overplayed that hand as a society? I don’t think we, as a society, are capable of speaking out as one and declaring anything definitively good, bad, cool, dumb or otherwise. If you don’t like a mustache, that’s your business. I think the courage and self confidence it takes to only grow out the hair on your upper lip reflects something about what’s going on in your soul. Mustaches can be evil. They can be goofy. They can be stoic. They can be boring. They can represent the apex of what it means to be middling, no nonsense, run-of-the-mill accounting type or it can be the pièce de résistance on the most interesting man in the world. Masculinity is a spectrum upon which the mustache squarely sits. What do you think Keldon’s mustache says about him? Says he can pull off a hook shot in traffic, I’ll tell you that much.

stories.detailText: The NFL Honors ceremony is on the move, again. The made-for-TV awards show, which shifts this year from broadcast to streaming, will also be sliding back to its original day. John Ourand of Puck reports that NFL Honors will be held not on the Thursday of Super Bowl week but on the Saturday of Super Bowl weekend. The show slid to Thursday in 2022. Netflix has acquired the rights to the show, which attracted 3.7 million viewers in February 2026. During the event, the various Associated Press awards are announced. Also, the new class of Hall of Famers is unveiled. As NFL programming goes, the numbers aren't great. As live TV goes, three million people at one time is nothing to sneeze at. Whether Netflix will realize that kind of audience remains to be seen — if the official figure is even disclosed. Regardless, the show will quickly be forgotten as the NFL pivots the next day to the biggest event of the year.

stories.title: RAMalytics: How will Rams deploy their new offensive wrinkle?
stories.summary: Rams helped their passing game with “pony personnel”. Can they also find momentum in the run game?
stories.detailText: Sean McVay looked at the Los Angeles Rams’ depth chart following their recent rash of injuries and said “I’m just going to put our best remaining players on the field.” At times Sunday against the Arizona Cardinals, that meant deploying both Blake Corum and Kyren Williams at the same time . Two-back sets, commonly referred to as “pony personnel”, unlocked LA’s passing game despite a limited corps of pass catchers. McVay’s wrinkle was to play with three tight ends in lieu of having a receiver on the field. This wasn’t 21 or 22 personnel. It was 20 (two backs, no receivers). The interesting part? 207 (89%) of the Rams’ 234 passing yards came with both Corum and Williams on the field while 12 yards and 15 yards came from 11 and 13 personnel groupings, respectively. Matthew Stafford was 13 of 17 on such plays. In the Rams’ bread and butter 13 personnel? He completed just three of six passes for 15 yards and took a sack. It’s mildly strange that the Rams leaned into the passing game with two backs on the field. They had little rushing production to show for it otherwise. Out of LA’s 202 rushing yards, 19 came from the 20 personnel. They ran 40 times for 183 yards out of 13 personnel, and then netted zero yards between 12 and 21. This is a dichotomy that must be assessed and bridged together. If McVay’s newest offensive wrinkle is going to have staying power, the next step is to also threaten on the ground. There should be plenty of opportunities for changeups and misdirection based on the tape LA left for opponents against Arizona. It remains to be seen whether the two-back sets are a means to getting by without Puka Nacua and Davante Adams. LA could brush the idea aside once their receiver room returns to health. Or, as we saw last season, the Rams may be finding lightning in a bottle that will eventually be emulated by the rest of the NFL. At least for now, Sean McVay has our attention. His inventiveness is trademarked. How long is the runway for the newest trick up his sleeve?

stories.title: 49ers WR Mike Evans' Achilles tendinitis injury explained
stories.summary: ESPN spoke with a medical professional for a better understanding of Evans' diagnosis. When could he return? And will the injury completely resolve itself?
stories.detailText: COLORADO SPRINGS, Colo. -- As wide receiver Mike Evans works his way back from Achilles tendinitis , nobody in the San Francisco 49ers ' locker room knows better how frustrating that injury can be than running back Christian McCaffrey . In 2024, McCaffrey missed the first eight games of the season with bilateral Achilles tendinitis -- tendinitis in both legs, though the issue was more concentrated to one of his legs. The injury still makes him wince at the mere mention of it. "It's tough," McCaffrey said. "It's a compounding thing that can get worse really quickly and then it can be really debilitating. I had my own experience with it. I hated everything about it." While Evans isn't dealing with the bilateral version of the injury -- his tendinitis is in his right leg -- the issue has been enough to keep him out of three-plus games. His last play came in the second quarter of the 49ers' Week 6 win over the Commanders, and he had missed practice all week leading up to that game with Achilles soreness and a rib issue. There's still no definitive return date for Evans, though coach Kyle Shanahan said before Week 10 that Evans has progressed well and has "a chance" to return as soon as Sunday night against the Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City. "I'm hoping to, just not sure yet. Still too early," Shanahan said Monday when asked if Evans will be back at practice this week. "He's flying in tonight with the guys who were left behind who didn't travel with us to Dallas. So we'll let these next few days go and see if he can get out there sometime this week." While the 49ers' offense has still been good without Evans, averaging 6.4 yards per play without him, it's been downright dominant with him. The Niners are averaging 7.2 yards per play with Evans on the field this season. Without Evans, the 49ers are Super Bowl contenders. With him, they could be the favorites. "Everybody on the field, their life is easier because of how good he is and how much of a threat he is," tight end George Kittle said. "I've actually never been more confident in an offense than when I look out and I see Mike Evans ... I'm excited to get Mike back, hopefully." For the Niners, it's not just about getting back their No. 1 receiver. It's about getting Evans back and keeping him back upon his return. ESPN spoke to Dr. Daniel Kaplan, an orthopedic surgeon at NYU Langone Hospital, to discuss the nature of Evans' injury, the timeline for him to return, and whether the injury can be completely resolved so he's able to finish the season without issue. Dr. Kaplan has not treated Evans' injury specifically nor does he work with the Niners. (The conversation has been edited for brevity and clarity.) Mike Evans is dealing with Achilles tendinitis; can you explain what it is and any potential causes? Kaplan: Tendinitis is in the family of overwork usage injury. It's not like a tear or something like that. It's usually a chronic ongoing inflammation of the tendon. It's about load and load management. Usually when it becomes persistent, it goes slightly from tendinitis to tendinosis, which is not just inflammation but when some of the tissue is a little bit less healthy. It's not necessarily at risk for rupture, but it just means it takes a little bit longer for things to heal. And he's probably -- given the fact that he has been out for a couple weeks now -- in that territory. You mentioned it's not necessarily at more risk of rupture, but what are the risks of attempting to play through it or push it before it's fully healthy? Kaplan: The biggest risk is really more that you let this thing perpetuate and just not actually cool down. So instead of getting 100% better, you're 75% better and then you play and now you're 70% better. That's the bigger risk. Theoretically, whenever a tendon is not working optimally or a tendon around it, you are just in general at slightly higher risk. It's not that he's at no increased risk, but that's just not the primary concern. Generally speaking, what is the recovery timeline for Achilles tendinitis? Kaplan: It totally depends on the severity. Also, timing in the season. If it's like the Super Bowl, he's playing because it's mostly about a pain thing as opposed to necessarily a function aspect. We usually assume it's in the two- to four-week range for tendinitis. That's about what I would expect. Longer than that sometimes, but a lot of it has to do with how much he's actually shut down. It sounds like they did the right thing by actually shutting him down, as opposed to the other option is trying to play through it and letting it drag on and then it's just never going to resolve. So, it's an injury that if you treat it properly, it can resolve in that time and not linger all season? Kaplan: Exactly. It is like an overuse workload thing. He's a wide receiver. Explosive. He's running a million sprints in practice every day type of thing. You don't just purely shut them down and just have them sit on the couch. There's a physical therapy component where you're doing certain types of strengthening and stretching and things like that. You are trying to reduce the inflammation. So that's anti-inflammatories, that's cold baths, that's massage. It's not that you're just purely saying, "Don't play for three weeks and you'll be fine." There is an active treatment component to it, but the most important thing is giving the tendon a break. McCaffrey had bilateral Achilles tendinitis a couple of years ago, and he missed eight games. Does bilateral versus one leg make a difference in recovery or does it depend on how they handled recovery more? Kaplan: I wouldn't think so. That timeline was way longer for McCaffrey than I would expect for this problem. I would expect it wasn't necessarily that the problem was bilateral, just more the severity. Once Evans' injury resolves, is he then at higher risk for it to return or is that solely dependent on usage? Kaplan: Mostly just depending on usage. Now, if he's prone to it for some sort of biomechanical reason, I suppose it's possible. But to my knowledge, it's not like that's something that he has been battling over the course of his career. So, I don't think so as long as it does resolve. And that's where the secret sauce comes in about really determining when it's safe for him to go back because you obviously don't want to keep him out any longer than you have to. But if you send him back too soon, then you restart the clock and now all of a sudden, it's another two weeks here, another week there. It's kind of like when people have hamstring tears and you follow those; it's the same idea.

stories.title: Mike McCarthy on Steelers' blowout loss: 'Needs to stop there'
stories.summary: After a deflating loss at Cincinnati, Pittsburgh faces a Week 11 gut-check game at the Eagles on Sunday.
stories.detailText: PITTSBURGH -- In the wake of a 20-point loss Sunday night, Pittsburgh Steelers linebacker Patrick Queen was soft-spoken and introspective as he outlined two paths forward for his team. "I think, for the most part, all of us are looking at ourselves and just knowing where we could have been better, what we could have done just to stop the bleeding here and there," he said. "The other way you could look at it is [that] it goes downhill, and we can just keep going downhill the whole season." Monday afternoon, Steelers coach Mike McCarthy emphatically chose the former. "This needs to be one game, and it needs to stop there," McCarthy said. "... This is a part of the journey of the season, but it needs to be one game, and that'll be our approach as we prepare for Philadelphia." After a deflating 38-18 Week 10 loss , the Steelers face a Week 11 gut-check game at the Eagles on Sunday ( 1 p.m. ET, CBS ). But just because McCarthy needs the loss to be a one-game speed bump in the Steelers' season doesn't mean it will be -- especially facing a cross-state rival in a city where the Steelers haven't won a regular-season game since 1965. And though the Steelers had a history of resilience under former coach Mike Tomlin and posted a 12-2 record in games following a loss of 20 or more points, McCarthy's units haven't rebounded as successfully. McCarthy is 8-15 in games following a loss of at least 20 points, including a 2-8 record in Dallas. Even so, McCarthy dismissed the idea Sunday night that the loss could turn the tide of the season. "Oh, wow," he said, somewhat incredulous at the question. "It's one loss, and it will be dealt with as much. I'm more focused on the details of the fundamentals and the things we needed to do. "We're not going to drive down the drama road of those types of things. It's a waste of time. It's a waste of energy, and we're going to pour our energy into ourselves looking in the mirror and stay focused on the things that we can control." The Steelers did that after each of their previous losses and responded with wins, including a four-game streak after the Thursday night loss in Cleveland during Week 4. But Sunday night's loss at Cincinnati felt different. A win against one of the league's hottest teams could have legitimized Pittsburgh's 6-2 start to a national audience, solidified its standing as a serious postseason contender and validated a series of front office decisions, including bringing back quarterback Aaron Rodgers this offseason and also standing pat at this month's NFL trade deadline. Though they entered Cincinnati as underdogs, the Steelers had reason to believe they could prove the sportsbooks wrong. Teams coming off a bye were undefeated in games against opponents who played in an international game the previous week. McCarthy was 12-6 after bye weeks. And perhaps most crucially, the Steelers beat the Bengals 30-27 seven weeks earlier. Instead, the Steelers were thoroughly dismantled and outplayed by Cincinnati in every phase. They were outgained by 262 yards, their worst margin in nearly three decades. Rodgers opened the game with a career-worst eight incompletions before finally connecting with tight end Darnell Washington late in the second quarter. And the Steelers' formidable edge rushers didn't record a quarterback pressure or sack on a near-flawless Joe Burrow , while Rodgers was sacked three times and hit six times total. "The biggest thing this week was handling how to win and coming off a four-game win streak and then we had a bye," Steelers left tackle Troy Fautanu said. "We were fresh. There was no real excuse for us going out there and performing like this. We just got to get better." That starts with another week of introspection and self-improvement. After the Week 4 loss to the Browns, McCarthy's mandate to his players was to clean up their house. This week, the Steelers have to break out the brooms and dustpans again. "Our toughness didn't go away because we got beat last week," Pittsburgh defensive coordinator Patrick Graham said Monday. "Our resiliency didn't go away because we got beat yesterday. We lost the game. We didn't play the way we wanted to play. We didn't coach the way we wanted to coach, and they beat us. "... We're going to pull closer together and get the answers and go out there. And we got a great opportunity this week against Philadelphia, against a team that's fighting right now an in-state rivalry, and it's going to provide some spark there. "But we got plenty of motivation to get it right as opposed to going the other route."

stories.title: 49ers rookie Kaelon Black has developed RB tandem with Christian McCaffrey
stories.summary: The San Francisco 49ers' run game is one of the best in the league, thanks to the tandem of Christian McCaffrey and rookie Kaelon Black.
stories.detailText: The San Francisco 49ers wanted to develop rookie running back Kaelon Black in order preserve Christian McCaffrey , decreasing the amount of carries he has on a game-to-game basis. McCaffrey is going to be McCaffrey, no matter what. However, it's Black, the 25-year-old rookie who has filled into that role just as the Niners had hoped when they took him with the 90th overall pick in the third round of the 2026 NFL Draft . Black has been the perfect complement to McCaffrey throughout the season. Together, they've piled up 1,323 scrimmage yards and 15 touchdowns on 239 attempts through nine games. Black has 373 yards and two touchdowns on 84 carries. 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan has been impressed with Black's development and how McCaffrey took him under his wings the moment he came into the team facility. "I also think Christian really respects Kaelon," Shanahan told reporters on Nov. 16. "I remember Christian telling me right when he got here how much of a pro that guy seemed like and seemed like he was made of the right stuff. It's because K.B., similar to Christian, he works at everything. He's very hard on himself. He's very tough and approaches each day to get better. As talents and as people, I think they pair together very well." The two continued to show why they're quietly becoming one of the better backfield tandems in the league. In the Week 10 matchup against the Dallas Cowboys , Black and McCaffrey combined for 289 yards and four touchdowns. While McCaffrey ran for 62 yards and a touchdown, he also added four catches on four targets for a career-high 161 yards and two touchdowns. “I think Christian's the perfect mentor just because even if he doesn't say anything, just how Christian works every second," Shanahan said. "Christian's the most detailed, focused, obsessive player I've ever been around. Just watch how he blocks when [WR] Deebo's [Samuel Sr.] running back and he's playing receiver and just the technique and the effort he goes through on every single play. Just the way Christian plays football is the best example or mentor to anybody who’s on our team or anybody who wants to watch how a football player goes about his business." 49ERS-COWBOYS WINNERS AND LOSERS Purdy, McCaffrey lead 49ers offense in high-scoring win Black is learning from McCaffrey. He was targeted twice and caught both passes for 13 yards. On the ground, he had 11 touches for 53 yards and a touchdown, scoring on a 25-yard bruising run during which Black trucked through the Cowboys' secondary. Shanahan praised Black for his physicality on the field whether running the ball or blocking for teammates. “Oh, it was awesome. The one I got to see live was running over the safety, and the safety brought it too," Shanahan said. "I thought that was a good play by the safety, but K.B. brought it more. Then to finish it on the corner was such an impressive run." "I didn't get to see his chips on the D-Lineman live," he added. "I saw [Dallas Cowboys DL] Quinnen Williams go out in the game and they told me that was because K.B. hit him and I was trying to figure out how he did because it was on a bootleg. Then he did it another time on another player going through the B-gap, so just the physicality he looks for and then the way his body's wired that when you have that mentality and you're wired that way, obviously when he hits them it feels a little bit different." While Black did have a mind-blowing fumble towards the end of the game while the Cowboys were desperately trying to mount a comeback, the 49ers retained possession. Shanahan praised Cowboys defensive lineman Quinnen Williams for lodging the ball out, rather criticizing his rookie running back. "We'll see if he was loose with or if he had his elbow up, if he didn't have his pressure points," Shanahan said. "From what I saw on the sideline 92 is a big man, got his arm in there and just raked it out, so we got to see how he was holding it and stuff, but it was a good play by 92 and I;m glad that we recovered it because it could have been a big one." Black's play throughout the season has gained the trust of his coaches and teammates. He's showing why the Niners selected him. McCaffrey had 1,222 scrimmage yards and 8 touchdowns on 229 touches through nine games in 2025. This season in the same amount of games, his touches are way down at 155. McCaffrey has gained 950 scrimmage yards and scored 13 touchdowns through nine games. Those other touches went to Black, whose progressing along quite nicely as a rookie alongside McCaffrey. They've helped the Niners become one of the best running teams in the NFL. San Francisco is ranked fifth in rush yards (1,296), third in rush touchdowns (15) and third in yards per carry (4.9). stories.title: Monday Night Football: Chargers lead Ravens 17-10 at halftime
stories.summary: Justin Herbert and Omarion Hampton have touchdown runs for the winless Chargers.
stories.detailText: The Chargers lead the Ravens 17-10 at halftime on Monday. That is more points than the winless Chargers have scored in five games and the same as they scored in a 23-17 loss to the Broncos. They scored 23 against Seattle and 22 last week against Houston. Los Angeles scored on 3-of-5 first-half possessions, getting a 22-yard touchdown run from Justin Herbert, a 38-yard Cameron Dicker field goal and a 1-yard Omarion Hampton touchdown run. Hampton's touchdown came on fourth-and-goal with 1:56 remaining in the half. Roquan Smith initially had Hampton stopped before the running back got a push from offensive lineman Cole Strange and a pull from fullback Scott Matlock. Officials should have penalized Matlock for the pull, as pulling is illegal. The Chargers outgained the Ravens 175 to 161, with Baltimore having no rushing yards on six carries. Herbert, who injured his left hand in last week's loss to the Texans but wasn't on the injury report this week, went 6-for-9 for 91 yards in the first half. He also ran for 45 yards on six carries. Hampton has 36 yards on 10 carries, and Tre' Harris has five catches for 86 yards. Jacoby Brissett, making his first start for the Ravens after the trade from Arizona, has completed 14 of 23 passes for 163 yards and an interception. Del'Shawn Phillips had the pick on a pass that was behind Ja'Kobi Lane and deflected to the Chargers linebacker. Derrick Henry has a 2-yard touchdown run, but he has minus-1 yard on five carries. Mark Andrews has four catches for 41 yards.

stories.title: Rams center Coleman Shelton out 4-6 weeks with hamstring injury
stories.summary: Coleman Shelton strained his hamstring in the second quarter of the Rams' Week 10 victory over the Cardinals.
stories.detailText: LOS ANGELES -- Rams center Coleman Shelton strained his hamstring and is expected to sit out the next four to six weeks, a team spokesperson said Monday. Shelton sustained the injury in the second quarter of the Rams' Week 10 victory over the Arizona Cardinals . He had not missed an offensive snap this season for the Rams before his injury. Shelton was replaced at center by Dylan McMahon , who played only nine offensive snaps before he injured his knee. The Rams said Monday that McMahon partially tore his patellar tendon and will be put on injured reserve. Offensive lineman Beaux Limmer moved to center after McMahon's injury, and backup offensive lineman Bill Murray moved to left guard, playing 49 offensive snaps. The injuries are just the latest for a Rams offense that is also currently without wide receivers Puka Nacua and Davante Adams , tight end Terrance Ferguson , and guard Steve Avila . The Rams, 6-4 after winning four games in a row, are on their bye this week. They host the Green Bay Packers in Week 12.

stories.title: Dolphins cut kicker Zane Gonzalez a day after costly misses in loss to Colts
stories.summary: The Dolphins waived kicker Zane Gonzalez on Monday, a day after he missed two field goals and an extra point in a 24-22 loss to the Colts.
stories.detailText: MIAMI GARDENS, Fla. -- The Dolphins waived kicker Zane Gonzalez , a day after a series of missed kicks hindered Miami in a 24-22 loss to the Indianapolis Colts . Gonzalez joined the Dolphins in Week 7 after the team released Riley Patterson but missed kicks in three consecutive games -- including two field goals and an extra point in Sunday's loss to Indianapolis. Speaking to reporters after the game, Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley was blunt in his assessment of how the missed kicks impacted the game's outcome. "We got to make the extra point, and we got to make the field goals," Hafley said. "I'm not going to ever B.S. you. It's 24-22. A missed extra point forces us to go for two, and we missed two field goals. That's seven points. We have to make those." Dolphins special teams coordinator Chris Tabor said last week that he still "had a lot of confidence" in Gonzalez, and suggested he was still acclimating after missing the first six weeks of the season. He made two of three field goal attempts against the New England Patriots in Week 8, before hitting three of four attempts against the Detroit Lions last week. Gonzalez made a 53-yard field goal Sunday, but missed from 47 yards and 51 yards, including a go-ahead kick early in the fourth quarter. "You look at the misses, you look at why he missed and what he's done in the body of work and the time that we've had him and you give him a shot and that's what we did," Hafley said Monday. "And that was the decision that was made. And unfortunately, the results weren't very good this week, and now we're going to find another kicker." Hafley said the Dolphins had a pair of available kickers in mind and would make a decision later this week. The team has tried out multiple kickers over the past several weeks, including former All-Pros Daniel Carlson and Justin Tucker . Also, defensive tackle Zeek Biggers will have season-ending knee surgery to repair his lateral meniscus, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport on Monday night.

stories.title: Von Miller blames himself, not the play call, for Christian McCaffrey's late TD
stories.summary: The Cowboys pulled within 38-32 of the 49ers with 3:42 left in the fourth quarter on Sunday.
stories.detailText: The Cowboys pulled within 38-32 of the 49ers with 3:42 left in the fourth quarter on Sunday. Only 19 seconds later, Christian McCaffrey was celebrating in the end zone. Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker is under fire for calling cover zero on second-and-10. He sent a six-man blitz, leaving man-to-man coverage and Von Miller matched up with McCaffrey. McCaffrey called it " a perfect look for that play ." The running back ran a seam route, quickly got a step (or two or three) on the 37-year-old edge rusher, caught the ball at the 40 and was off to the races. Miller reached 18.5 mph while chasing McCaffrey, but it wasn't fast enough. Miller, though, defended Parker and the play call on Monday. “As a defensive coordinator in that situation, you want to be aggressive ,” Miller said, via Nick Harris of the Fort Worth Star-Telegram . “We were trying to win the game. We were trying to create momentum. We were down by six points. If we could have just got off the field. . . . As a defensive coordinator, you want to be aggressive and want to win the game. That’s the type of mindset you want in these games.” Parker is three years younger than Miller, but has Miller's full support despite the struggles of the Cowboys defense. Dallas allowed 584 yards to the 49ers. “Nah, that’s crazy,” Miller said of the calls for Parker's job. “Christian is an incredible leader of men. All of these offensive and defensive coordinators are geniuses. It’s really getting your players to buy in. What happened with me yesterday is a microcosm of what has happened the whole season. Instead of me looking for a simpler way to do that job, I have to find a better way to do it. That had nothing to do with Christian Parker. I had been coached on how to play that route. I’ve had examples of that route, went over that play in practice this week. I just didn’t make that play. That had nothing to do with Christian Parker. I just didn’t execute."

stories.title: Rams starting center Coleman Shelton to be sidelined for weeks
stories.summary: Rams center Coleman Shelton sustained a hamstring strain against the Arizona Cardinals and will be out four to six weeks.
stories.detailText: Rams center Coleman Shelton stands on the field before a win over the Chargers. (Kyusung Gong / Associated Press) For much of the season, the Rams’ offensive line avoided the injury barrage that sidelined multiple key players. Not anymore. Center Coleman Shelton will be sidelined four to six weeks and guard/center Dylan McMahon will be placed on injured reserve after suffering hamstring and knee injuries, respectively, during the Rams’ 34-6 victory over the Arizona Cardinals, a team official said Monday. Read more: Sean McVay showcases his ability to adapt in Rams’ blowout win over Cardinals Shelton left the game in the second quarter because of a hamstring strain and was replaced by McMahon, who subsequently suffered a torn patella that forced him to leave the game. Beaux Limmer , who was making his first start at left guard in place of injured Steve Avila, moved to center, and Bill Murray replaced Limmer at guard. Shelton, 31, is an eighth-year pro and a pillar for a line that has given up 15 sacks, tied for sixth fewest in the NFL. Limmer, a 2024 sixth-round pick from Arkansas, started 14 games at center as a rookie but struggled in the NFC divisional-round defeat by the Philadelphia Eagles. Avila suffered a hamstring injury during the Rams’ Nov. 8 victory over the Washington Commanders, and initially was expected to be sidelined for four weeks. Rookie lineman Keagen Trost was activated from injured reserve a few weeks ago. Guard Justin Dedich has been on injured reserve since the start of the season because of a non-football related hand injury. The Rams do not play again until Nov. 25, when they will host the Green Bay Packers. stories.title: Andy Reid defends Xavier Worthy, who had no catches in 57 snaps
stories.summary: Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes completed 22 passes to eight different receivers and threw five touchdowns in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Falcons.
stories.detailText: Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes completed 22 passes to eight different receivers and threw five touchdowns in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Falcons. None of his completions went to Xavier Worthy. Worthy has 33 catches for 278 yards and a touchdown in nine games this season. The Chiefs have not used him in the run game. On Sunday, he led all Kansas City wide receivers with 57 snaps and drew three targets. He also made a special teams mistake, allowing the Falcons to recover the first successful onside kick of the season in the NFL. Coach Andy Reid was asked about Worthy's lack of production, which had to be at least part of the reason the Chiefs traded for Josh Downs last week. Downs had four catches for 53 yards and a touchdown in his Kansas City debut. “He just needs to keep doing his thing and working, and he’ll be fine ,” Reid said Monday, via Charles Goldman of AtoZ Sports. “Some days will be his, and some days it goes to other guys. I mean, that’s just how this thing works. We’re spreading it around. Pat loves spreading it around and does a great job with it. Our coaches love doing that. It’s tough on defenses. Everybody’s kind of getting a little piece of the pie. You saw when he was only the guy against the Chargers and his production there was great. So, it’s not that he’s not capable of that.” Reid further explained that the Falcons' game plan was to take Worthy out of the game, which "allowed other guys to be available." Worthy, a first-round pick in 2024, had his best season as a rookie when he made 59 catches for 638 yards and six touchdowns, while also running for 104 yards and three touchdowns on 20 carries. In the 23 games he's played since, Worthy has 75 catches for 810 yards and two touchdowns, with 11 carries for 87 yards and no touchdowns.

stories.title: The Packers’ offensive line regressed against the Vikings
stories.summary: Mental mistakes really did Green Bay in early in the game
stories.detailText: (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images We all saw the Green Bay Packers’ offensive line get pushed around by the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday, but I’m sure some of you are wondering exactly why the team messed up in crucial situations over and over. Hopefully, you’ll learn a little more about the game and the status of the team by the end of this article. I want to start with this up front: I don’t think the Packers’ running game was actually that bad on Sunday — at least on the relative scale of Green Bay’s running game. Where I really think the team regressed was in the pass protection department, where they played their worst game since at least the first three weeks of the season. Let’s start with the run game. Running Game Kaleb Johnson carries Counter: +3 Duo: +2 OZ: +1 Counter: +3 Sweep: -2 Counter: +6 Split Zone: +8 Counter: +9 Split Zone: +4 Long Trap: +8 pic.twitter.com/9gPWu2c1xC — Justis Mosqueda (@JuMosq) November 16, 2026 MarShawn Lloyd carries: Counter: +11 Counter: +4 Long trap?: -3 Counter: +1 pic.twitter.com/jJFd9vKZ77 — Justis Mosqueda (@JuMosq) November 16, 2026 Chris Brooks carries: Insert: 0 Counter: +1 pic.twitter.com/Freia8Srpz — Justis Mosqueda (@JuMosq) November 16, 2026 I clipped up all of the runs that the Packers’ running backs had in the tweets above, if you want to check them out. There are a couple of poor calls (like the pin and pull sweep that had no chance because of Minnesota’s defensive call), but for the most part, Green Bay got a hat on a hat against the Vikings, something we can’t say of prior games. Can they move anyone? No! They never have been able. They have one preferred starter on the field. Can they get in front of people, at least on the ground? The last two weeks are probably the Packers’ best back-to-back performances this season. The first big mistake the Packers made was on this duo run. The diagram above is what Green Bay’s offensive line is expecting pre-snap. Because the Vikings stunted their three-technique defensive lineman outside on the play, though, right tackle Anthony Belton never gets off his block, and there’s a free runner when the play should have gotten up to the safety level. It’s the second play in the Johnson cutup . The second big mess-up was on this outside zone toss, where the team handled another stunt poorly. On paper, if everyone stays in the gaps they line up in, the diagram above is what the run should look like. Essentially, offensive linemen try to “scoop” defensive linemen to their play-side, and if there isn’t a defender in that gap, they climb to the second level and try to work on backers and safeties, after first securing that no one stunted in their play-side gap pre-snap. The problem is that the Vikings don’t stay in their gaps, and they slant weak on the play. Because of this, there should be three pass-offs. The Packers don’t execute a single one of them, leading to all three players getting penetration. let's check in on the Packers' run blocking pic.twitter.com/lX7D1OOU2z — Benjamin Solak (@BenjaminSolak) November 16, 2026 It’s the play that you keep seeing screenshots of over and over again. It’s the fourth play in the Johnson cutup. These plays look like crap, but outside of that, the Packers mostly played their rules correctly this week — again, which has not been the case over most of the year. Over the last two weeks, they’ve found something that worked for them: running counter, a play that allows the offensive linemen to get on train tracks and just block downhill instead of worrying about assignments being exchanged by the Vikings’ blitzes and stunts. Everyone makes a wall of down blocks except for a kickout player (either a pulling guard or a tight end) and an insert player (again, either a pulling guard or tight end). As a reminder, the zone plays that didn’t work against Minnesota are what Green Bay ran a lot of in the preseason and through Week 3 of the regular season. They went out of their way to try to get good at what they’re doing the worst this year. I didn't remember the wingback counter coming off Pierre Strong playing QB lol pic.twitter.com/Oi1382F4VV — Justis Mosqueda (@JuMosq) November 10, 2026 On counter and split zone concepts, the Packers had 10 carries for 50 yards (5 yards per carry) on the day. On other concepts, which mostly relied on changing targets post-snap, the Packers were just 6 for 6 (1 YPC). My guess: Green Bay wanted to punish Minnesota with the ground game this week, particularly counter and split zone runs, but the game got out of hand and they had to ditch that script when they were down three scores. The team played a lot of extra tight end looks in this game , allowing the Vikings to get an extra player in the box on defense. Passing Game The passing game is really where the Packers’ line struggled, in part because they were playing these multiple tight end sets that added just another variable for Green Bay’s line to account for. Against Minnesota, the Packers looked completely lost on the interior offensive line, which was made up of Laken Tomlinson, John Williams and Travis Glover (left to right). I thought we were over this. From Weeks 4-9, after the disaster that was the Atlanta Falcons game on Monday Night Football , the Packers had just a 35 pressure rate, good for the 16th-lowest in the NFL over this time. They looked like an average pass-protection unit over the last two months. In the first three weeks of the year, the Packers cracked the 40 percent pressure rate twice, but had done it only once in the past six weeks. It seemed like they turned a corner, but then the Vikings came to town. Yesterday, Minnesota posted a 60 percent pressure rate, the highest number that Green Bay has allowed all season. In Weeks 1-3 and 10, the Packers have allowed a 46 percent pressure rate overall, the highest mark in the league over those four weeks. It’s hard to know what Green Bay’s offensive line will look like moving forward , because we just saw a huge regression after a streak of solid play. Mind you, this all came with Love’s time to throw at just 2.27 seconds against the Vikings, and they still sacked him eight times in this game. For perspective, the average NFL time to throw is around 2.8 seconds, so Love was operating about a half-second faster than the average. And he was still getting popped left and right. Had he held onto the ball at an average rate, the line’s pressure rate would have been even higher. Here are just a few clips of the Packers’ offensive line blowing up plays from essentially the snap of the ball on Sunday, just to show how poor it was: Tight formation allows MIN to get 9 in the box. Dallas Turner is never touched by Mekhi Becton. Love hit blindside pic.twitter.com/XL0DZct61t — Justis Mosqueda (@JuMosq) November 16, 2026 Packers 7 for 5 in protection in this tight 3 TE set (Becton at TE again). Either Becton or Glover doesn't pick up former Packer Eric Wilson on the delayed blitz pic.twitter.com/ZuavJeKvbZ — Justis Mosqueda (@JuMosq) November 16, 2026 Becton is dual reading 61 and 43. Jonnu's chip does nothing. Love has to step up into the guy John Williams lost to one-on-one. pic.twitter.com/lPG55Zpzro — Justis Mosqueda (@JuMosq) November 16, 2026 This tweet is supposed to say Belton, not Becton. I apologize to the Becton family. Belton loses on athleticism (should be a guard in the NFL) and Williams + Becton just blow their blocks. Jordan Love sacked pic.twitter.com/sda9P4MjPe — Justis Mosqueda (@JuMosq) November 16, 2026 John Williams had the best seat in the house to watch the game on Sunday pic.twitter.com/dcIHCNm1np — Justis Mosqueda (@JuMosq) November 16, 2026 Packers iOL is supposed to be 3 for 3 and loses all 3 pic.twitter.com/C6dmWsh2ho — Justis Mosqueda (@JuMosq) November 16, 2026 Lloyd is probably supposed to cross block here (Packers would have still been in a 1 for 2 because they let the Vikings walk up 8 with their formation width) pic.twitter.com/MscsDtPJGP — Justis Mosqueda (@JuMosq) November 16, 2026 All three interior offensive linemen had disaster games, looking consistently confused by Minnesota’s defense. Right tackle also Anthony Belton struggled, as he’s not a good athlete for the tackle position and should ideally be a guard at this level — but the injury to Zach Bako-Bewele forced him into his position this year. — Green Bay’s plan to add extra bodies into the formation with multiple tight end sets kind of worked in the run game, where they were able to run counter and split zone runs pretty well against Minnesota, but they couldn’t stick with the ground game once they went down multiple points — understandably. What really hurt on the ground was when the offensive line had to think and react to the Vikings’ defensive front, and the line wasn’t able to execute on those runs. To make matters worse, the extra tight end (and offensive line) looks helped Minnesota bring an extra body in the box in the passing game, which adds exponentially more options for defensive coordinator Brian Flores for each body he could line up as a threat. Against those pressure fronts, the Packers’ interior offensive line’s heads were spinning all game. Next time, maybe LaFleur will want to spread out the formation against those pressure looks, instead of having running backs and tight ends walk up to the line of scrimmage. It’s what the Vikings did against Green Bay’s pressure fronts, and Minnesota was able to get a good number of explosive plays in those situations, notably on third and long. The Packers’ offensive line just isn’t good enough to deal with this many variables post-snap. They’re not coached well enough. LaFleur, the head coach, just hasn’t accepted that going into the second half of November. The offense looked better when they ditched their game plan in the second half of the third quarter, turning into a three-receiver spread team that ran the hurry-up no-huddle. The Packers went on a little run there and looked like they had a chance to get back into the game until they fumbled the ball on a kickoff return. The fact that “do what you want, just play fast” led to better results than Green Bay’s game plan is a damning indictment of the staff’s decisions this week.

stories.title: Jets QB Geno Smith avoids major injuries after leaving loss to Bills multiple times with concussion, ankle issue
stories.summary: The Jets fell to 2-8 on the season after Sunday's loss to the Bills.
stories.detailText: Though he left Sunday's contest multiple times with various injuries, Geno Smith appears to have avoided anything major. The New York Jets quarterback underwent tests on Monday that did not reveal any major issues, including on his ankle, according to the NFL Network's Ian Rapoport . Smith will continue to be evaluated this week, but he appears to be in a good spot to make the start again next Sunday for their contest against the Los Angeles Chargers. Smith left Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Buffalo Bills multiple times. He went down initially at the end of the first half when he was hit both high and low after throwing a pass, and he fell hard down to the ground on his back. He remained down for several moments before finally getting up and walking to the sideline medical tent. Geno Smith is down on the field pic.twitter.com/VITOuHm6J0 — Arye Pulli (@AryePulliNFL) November 15, 2026 Backup Cade Klubnik then took the field for the Jets to start the second half. Smith returned after clearing concussion protocol, but then left the game the following possession after a big hit. He was then sidelined with an ankle injury the rest of the way. Smith finished throwing 13-of-21 for 148 yards in the loss. Klubnik wasn't much better, and the Jets have now gone nine straight quarters without scoring a touchdown . Smith has thrown for 2,226 yards with 12 touchdowns and three interceptions this season, his first back with the Jets since 2016. The team holds just a 2-8 record and is well out of the playoff hunt already. They are well within range of securing the No. 1 overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft at this point, too. While the Jets haven't made a decision just yet, it sounds like Smith will be able to go in their matchup with the Chargers next weekend. The Chargers entered their Monday Night Football contest against the Baltimore Ravens as the league's only winless team, so Sunday will be a very big opportunity for Smith and the Jets to end their losing skid.

stories.detailText: Week 10 of the 2026 NFL season concludes on Monday Night Football, but Cleveland Browns fans get two weeks to relax and enjoy their team’s 6-4 start to the season and holding a current spot in the AFC Playoff picture. The bye week comes at a perfect time, according to HC Todd Monken, as the coaching staff will get a better chance to self-scout for the closing schedule. Perhaps that will help Cleveland start faster after the same concern has popped up week after week , including in their Week 10 victory over the Houston Texans . Either way, the time off will be good for the players’ bodies, while the coaches rework the plan. As of now, the Browns do not play again until November 29th at 1 PM against the Las Vegas Raiders. “As of now” is important, as the NFL can flex that game to Sunday Night Football instead of the early slot . That decision will have to be made by Tuesday. After facing the Raiders, with rookie QB Fernando Mendoza , Cleveland then welcomes the Cincinnati Bengals, the current AFC North leaders, and the Atlanta Falcons, led by their former head coach Kevin Stefanski, to finish off their four-game homestand. That leaves a finishing stretch with three out of four on the road: at the New York Giants, at the Baltimore Ravens, at home with the Indianapolis Colts, and finishing on the road against the Bengals again. Seven games, four at home and three on the road, starting with six wins on the record books coming out of the bye week. Some juicy storylines are included in that schedule as well. If the Browns can win two of the next three, Cleveland fans will start the 12 Days of Christmas with a clear sight of the NFL playoffs, and that is all we can ask for. stories.title: Cleveland Browns proving that TD passes may be overrated
stories.summary: Deshaun Watson has gone 4 straight games without a TD pass, but Cleveland has won three of them. So what’s the problem?
stories.detailText: (Photo by Jason Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Browns continued to befuddle the NFL on Sunday with their latest comeback victory. After falling behind 17-0 to the Houston Texans, the Browns did what they seem to do almost every week: the defense put a chokehold on the Texans, the offense slowly found its footing, and when Quinshon Judkins crossed the goal line with 53 seconds remaining, the Browns had their sixth victory of the season. No one can really explain how the Browns are doing it, not even the coaches or the players themselves, but they’re doing it because Cleveland has followed the same basic script in each of their six victories. Chief among the reasons that the Browns find themselves in a hole each week, but also one of the key reasons they have been able to overcome those deficits, has been the play of quarterback Deshaun Watson, who has generally been poor to bad for the first three quarters of each game, only to come alive in the fourth quarter. Deshaun Watson in final 2 minutes of 4th quarters this season 19 completions (t-most in NFL) 273 Pass Yards (most in NFL) 2 Pass TD (t-most in NFL) 0 INT (t-best in NFL) 141.8 Pass Rating (best in NFL) pic.twitter.com/DnYLKGMprV — PFF (@PFF) November 15, 2026 Watson has been especially effective in the final two minutes of games, as Pro Football Focus highlighted after Sunday’s win, as Watson is: Tied for the most completions (19) First in passing yards (273) Tied for the most touchdown passes (2) First in interceptions (0) First in passer rating (141.8) Tied for the most touchdown passes (2) That last bullet point is an interesting one, given a narrative that has emerged surrounding Watson, as his detractors are eager to point out that he has not thrown a touchdown pass since Week 5 against the New York Jets. But you know who did throw touchdown passes on Sunday? Cam Ward had two for the Tennessee Titans and lost Tyler Shough had one for the New Orleans Saints and lost Dak Prescott had five for the Dallas Cowboys and lost Aaron Rodgers had two for the Pittsburgh Steelers, and oh boy did they lose. Touchdown passes are fun and can make for great highlights, and there is no doubt Watson would love to have back that errant pass to Jerry Jeudy on Sunday that would have been a walk-in touchdown. But they are just one part of the bigger goal: outscore your opponent by any means necessary. Think back to the three touchdowns the Browns scored on Sunday: Watson had a six-yard run after hitting Jeudy on a 65-yard pass KC Concepcion had a six-yard run to finish a drive that included an 18-yard pass to Malachi Corley Judkins scored the game-winner on a five-yard run to finish a drive that featured a 30-yard completion to Harold Fannin Jr. Would it have made any difference if any of those scores had come on a pass instead of a run? Unless the NFL changes its rules overnight, a touchdown still counts as six points no matter how it is scored. Think back to all those times over the years when the Browns have been in a first-and-goal situation only to bumble their way into a turnover or settle for a field goal instead of a touchdown. The type of drive that goes something like a run on first down for minus-2 yards, a sack on second down, then an incompletion on third down that deflates a once-promising drive. At some point, Watson will throw another touchdown and another nonsensical narrative will die from a lack of oxygen. As long as the Browns finish more of their drives with touchdowns than field goals, does it really matter if they do it via the run or the pass? Bring the Dawg Pound with you on the SB Nation app! stories.title: Mike Macdonald says 'Sam's our quarterback' amid chatter that Drew Lock should start for Seahawks over Darnold
stories.summary: The Seahawks are now 4-0 this season with Lock, who's played objectively better than Sam Darnold in place of the injured Seattle starter in four appearances.
stories.detailText: Drew Lock threw for 240 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions Sunday as the Seattle Seahawks secured a 21-13 win over the Las Vegas Raiders . The Seahawks are now 4-0 this season with Lock, who's played objectively better than Sam Darnold in place of the injured Seattle starter in four appearances. This has prompted chatter amongst fans that maybe the Seahawks are better off with Lock as their full-time starting quarterback. 'Sam's our quarterback' That chatter reached head coach Mike Macdonald on Monday. He was quick to shoot down the idea during an interview with Seattle Sports radio . "Drew's been fantastic. He's been phenomenal," Macdonald said. "But Sam's our quarterback. … To have Drew as our backup and play the way he has has been awesome." What should the Seahawks do? It's an interesting spot for the Seahawks. Darnold had the second-best season of his career in his first season with Seattle last year, and the Seahawks won a Super Bowl. Seattle's defense and playmakers on offense in Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Kenneth Walker III were the primary driving forces of that championship run. But Darnold played his role well on a championship team. And moving away from a Super Bowl-winning quarterback the very next season could certainly be seen as a drastic step. Drew Lock has been objectively better than Sam Darnold this season. AP Photo/Reed Hoffmann Darnold has regressed But outside of last season and his 2024 campaign with the Minnesota Vikings, Darnold's body of work leaves a lot to be desired. A former No. 3 draft pick, Darnold was firmly in bust territory after bouncing around and failing to hold jobs with the Jets, Panthers and 49ers before landing in Minnesota. That version of Darnold is the one who's showed up in 2026. In seven starts this season, including the season-opener in which he played just one possession due to injury, Darnold's completed 60.2% of his passes for 7 yards per attempt with 10 touchdowns and 9 interceptions. Those are generally not numbers fitting of an NFL starter. The Seahawks are 2-4 in Darnold's starts excluding the season-opener, and his turnovers are a significant reason why. By comparison, Lock has completed 73.1% of his passes for 9 yards per attempt with 7 touchdowns and no interceptions. It's a small sample size from a career backup against a softer slate (Patriots, Cardinals, Cardinals, Raiders) than Darnold's faced (Commanders, Chargers, 49ers, Broncos, Chiefs, Bears). With two lost fumbles against the Raiders, Lock is not turnover free. But the numbers in his favor are compelling. Macdonald, meanwhile, had to stop himself short with his praise of Darnold Monday before shifting to attribute Darnold's struggles to injury. "We saw what Sam's been capable of both last year and in the — the beginning of the year for Sam has been a tough road," Macdonald said. … "Sam's our starting quarterback. I can't wait for him to be fully healthy probably for the first time." "Drew's been fantastic, but Sam's our quarterback...I can't for him to be fully healthy." #Seahawks HC Mike Macdonald explains why Sam Darnold will be the starter when the QB is healthy on w/ @BrockHuard & @TheMikeSalk . https://t.co/6070OwqdT0 pic.twitter.com/902XJBDgGC — Seattle Sports (@SeattleSports) November 16, 2026 The Seahawks have a bye this week. They'll come out of the bye for a key division showdown against the NFC-best 8-1 San Francisco 49ers on the other side. Macdonald told reporters Monday that the Seahawks are "optimistic" that Darnold will be ready to return from a quadriceps injury to face the 49ers. If he's healthy, expect Darnold to play. If he struggles in a Seahawks loss, expect this conversation to be renewed.

stories.summary: We go over the current NFC standings
stories.detailText: (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) | Getty Images The NFC playoff picture is set through ten weeks. The San Francisco 49ers are leading the way with one loss. Let’s take a look at the playoff picture: 1. San Francisco 49ers (8-1) 2. Detroit Lions (7-2, 1-0 vs CHI/MIN, 2-0 NFCN) 3. New York Giants (5-3-1) 4. Carolina Panthers (4-5) 5. Minnesota Vikings (7-2, 1-1 vs DET/CHI, win over CHI) 6. Chicago Bears (7-2, 0-2 vs DET/MIN, loss to MIN) 7. Green Bay Packers (6-4) 8. Seattle Seahawks (6-4, 2-1 NFCW) 9. Los Angeles Rams (6-4, 0-2 NFCW) 10. Dallas Cowboys (4-6) 11. Washington Commanders (3-5-1) 12. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-6, 3-3 NFC) 13. Arizona Cardinals (3-6, 2-5 NFC) 14. New Orleans Saints (3-6, 1-4 NFC) 15. Atlanta Falcons (3-7) 16. Philadelphia Eagles (2-7) In the NFC North, the three-way tie goes to the Detroit Lions because of their win over the Vikings. They are undefeated in the three-way head-to-head. The Vikings are next because they have a win over Chicago. The Vikings humbled the Packers in Week 10. Staying in the division, we still believe the Lions and Bears are the biggest threats to the 49ers. They have elite offenses, and we saw what happens when the Niners run into an aggressive passing attack. Unlike Dallas, Chicago and Detroit are just as dangerous on the ground as they are through the air. The Rams and Seahawks are still on the outside looking in. Green Bay currently holds the tiebreaker over Seattle based on best win percentage in conference games. It would be hilarious if the reason the reigning Super Bowl champs missed the playoffs was because they lost to Marcus Mariota. Speaking of the Commanders, they just beat the top team in their division. J.J. McCarthy looks lost against a 2-high structure, and their cornerbacks are bound to come back down to earth. A tie may be the reason New York sneaks into the playoffs. There’s a lot of football to be played. Another slip-up by the Giants opens the door for the Cowboys. If you rank the NFC by point differential, here’s how the standings would look: 49ers +85 Rams +61 Lions +58 Bears +57 Vikings +50 Seahawks +48 Buccaneers +24 I think it’d be easier to convince the masses that these are the conference’s seven best teams.

Behind Raiders fans' tribute to Fernando Mendoza's mother
teamStories.summary: Tom Joanides' social media campaign became a meaningful tribute when Mendoza scored in his first NFL start.
teamStories.detailText: HENDERSON, Nev. -- Las Vegas Raiders fan Tom Joanides, 46, had his first viral moment on social media for a good cause. He went on X asking Raiders fans, who were attending Sunday's game against the Seattle Seahawks at Allegiant Stadium, to stay seated after No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza scored his first touchdown. The idea was meant to honor Mendoza's mother, Elsa, who has been confined to a wheelchair due to her multiple sclerosis diagnosis. Watching the game at home with his family, Joanides saw thousands of Raiders fans remain in their seats while celebrating Mendoza's 10-yard touchdown run in the first quarter of his first career start. Elsa and Mendoza's father, Fernando Mendoza Sr., were seated in a suite, cheering on their son. "The fan base has an understanding that these are people; I'm shocked and elated that it actually happened. I've never had anything go viral ever," Joanides told ESPN. "But I'm not surprised that Raider Nation has the heart that it does." Despite the Raiders losing to the Seahawks 21-13 , Mendoza was "super grateful" for the fans' gesture, and it meant a lot to his family. "On a dark day, that brings a smile to my face," Mendoza said postgame . In July, Joanides, a Los Angeles native, went on X and wrote a post, asking fans to stay seated whenever Mendoza scored his first touchdown at home. However, his post didn't receive much traction . "I don't have a huge account or anything, so I was like yelling into the void," Joanides said. Five days before the Raiders' home matchup, Joanides went on X to reshare his message from the summer. This time, the fan base heard him. Joanides' post received more than 800,000 views and close to 400 reposts. Joanides, who began attending Raiders games with his dad when he was 3, said he would list "Raider Nation" as his ethnicity on government forms if he could. Joanides was inspired after watching a Front Office Sports interview , in which Mendoza said he donated $500,000 to the University of Miami Health System and the University of Miami Miller School of Medicine to help fight against multiple sclerosis. Mendoza's advocacy for the cause is inspired by Elsa, who was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis in 2008. His family launched the Mendoza Family Fund in April, which directly supports the National MS Society. Through their foundation, Mendoza's family has raised more than $1 million . "I just found it really touching," Joanides said. "This [was] an opportunity for this fan base to welcome [Mendoza] and his family in a very particular way and show what Raider Nation is all about."

teamStories.detailText: (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images Week 10 saw the Las Vegas Raiders lose their sixth game in seven tries, falling 21-13 to the Seattle Seahawks . But let’s check in on a few old friends and see how the weekend treated Kirk Cousins, Amik Robertson and Jakobi Meyers. Kirk Cousins Score: 30-10 Vikings win Stats: 21/31 (67.7%), 207 yards, 2 TDs, 1 INT, 3 rushes, 11 rushing yards Cousins didn’t get to practice with his new teammates until last Wednesday, but that was hard to tell on Sunday. He was very sharp and hit the ground running, allowing Minnesota to jump out to a 17-0 halftime lead in Green Bay. Justin Jefferson was certainly happy to see his old quarterback back, as Cousins targeted Jefferson 13 times, connecting for nine catches and 74 yards, the most catches and third-most yards the receiver has had in a single game this season. That helped the Vikings keep pace in the NFC North, as they’re tied with the Detroit Lions and Chicago Bears for first place at 7-2. Kirk Cousins man I’ll tell you what pic.twitter.com/5vX8egvFAM — Coach Dan Casey (@CoachDanCasey) November 15, 2026 Amik Robertson Score: 24-21 Commanders win Stats: 5 tackles, 2 TFLs, 1 PD This was a crazy game to start the weekend, as the Washington Commanders pulled off a comeback on Thursday Night Football to take down the division-leading New York Giants. Robertson was a big part of the effort, making a couple of notable plays against the run and coming up with a PBU. According to Pro Football Focus , he was targeted seven times and gave up four catches for 43 yards against the Giants. The 2020 fourth-round pick has quietly been having a good year with a career-high 75.7 PFF grade and an elite 90.1 mark against the run. Jakobi Meyers Score: 40-23 Jaguars win Stats: 3 catches, 34 yards Meyers didn’t have a big game on Sunday, but it’s been a while since we’ve checked in on him. The veteran receiver is far from the No. 1 target in Jacksonville, Parker Washington is, but he plays the role of a reliable safety net well. Fairly consistently, Meyers sits around 30 to 60 receiving yards per game and has totaled 26 catches for 374 yards and two touchdowns through nine games.
